tools.name: get_sites_overview
tools.description:
Get every Network site on one console with its device, client and health counts.

Reads POST /v2/api/sites/overview (a read-only query sent as a POST, so read-only
mode refuses it). Consequence: none intended; it changes nothing. Each site carries
id, name, description, counts (total/offline/wifi/wired/gateway devices,
wifi/wired/guest clients, pending updates, critical notifications, LAN/WAN/WiFi
configurations) and
percentages (wan_uptime, successful_association). Every page is drained by
default. Returns the first page's envelope as the upstream sent it (for example
total_page_count, total_element_count, page_number) with data holding the sites of
every page, plus _count (sites) and _pages (pages read); _incomplete and
_incompleteReason are added when the drain stopped short (a UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES
cap, a page without the paged envelope, or a page answered under another number).
A first page without a data array is returned as received. Pass page alone (0-based)
for that one page verbatim. page_size alone is window 0: exactly page_size sites
from the first; _nextPage counts page_size windows, so resume with page=_nextPage
and the same page_size. page with page_size returns that window of sites. _pageSize
reports the requested count, sent (every pageSize sent, in request order), the
effective console page size and the returned count. _nextPage is absent when no
site follows the window or the call stopped short (_incomplete). For counts across
every console use list_sites. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run",
dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends
nothing.

Required inputs: host.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

search_text.description: Filter sites by text, sent as searchText; for example "branch".

sort_by_field.description: Field to sort by, sent as sortByField; for example "name".

page.description:
Zero-based page. With page_size, returns exactly page_size records starting
at record page * page_size, gathered across console pages whatever the console
page size; resume with _nextPage and the same page_size. Without page_size, one
request returns that console page verbatim. For example 0.

page_size.description:
Number of sites. Alone, window 0 (the first page_size sites); with
page, the size of the window. Fewer if the collection ends. Omit to drain all.
Example: 1000.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: get_unified_ip_thread_topology
tools.description:
Project Matter nodes, Thread networks and the live IP topology into one view.

Required arguments: host, site. Reads matter/nodes, thread-networks and
topology/snapshot/live. Returns each body verbatim under _matterNodes, _threadNetworks and
_topologySnapshot, with _sources (path and outcome of each GET), _join (matterNodes,
threadBorderRouters, summary, notes) and _warnings (Thread timestamps are epoch
milliseconds). The join maps each Matter node by client_id (node_id when absent) to a
topology vertex, then to a Thread border router by normalized MAC, and gives every row a
joinState. A border router is linked to a Matter node only through a matched vertex; an

totalCount is the upstream total (null when none was reported). The first page's other envelope

stopped short.

`create_hotspot_vouchers`, `get_hotspot_voucher`, `delete_hotspot_voucher` — all
prefixed `hotspot_`. There is no shorter `list_vouchers`/`get_voucher` alias.

Vouchers are offset-paginated (native page size 100) and batches routinely
exceed that; by default every page is drained and all records are returned as
{data, totalCount}. Pass offset alone for a single manual page. A capped drain
is flagged incomplete.

The limit requests a total, gathered automatically in batches up to 1000;
_pageSize reports requested count, actual sent sizes per request,
observed effective size and returned count, without capping the total.

Required arguments: host, site.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

offset.description:
Optional zero-based starting record; alone, fetch one page manually.
Example: `25`.

limit.description:
Without offset, the record count gathered from the start in pages of at
most 1000; fewer only when the collection ends. With offset, limit is sent
unchanged as one page. The console clamps that page to 1000, so fewer can
return while more exist (compare _pageSize requested and returned). Omit
offset and limit to drain all.
Example: `25`.

filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as the
upstream `filter` query parameter for server-side filtering (e.g.
`name.like('*guest*')`). Omitted entirely when unset; applies when draining and
when paging manually.
Example: `name.eq('Conference')`.

success requires meta.rc "ok". With dry-run policy, returns the dry-run preview {status:

cmd as given and the controller judges it. The Network web app builds the rest of the body
at run time and its keys were not recovered from the 11.0.81 bundle, so params is free-form
and sent as given beside cmd (no key is added). Returns the Classic envelope {meta, data}
verbatim; success requires meta.rc "ok", otherwise the error carries the full upstream body.
With dry-run policy, returns the dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing. Consequence: build opens a shell
channel to the device; close ends it. Other action names execute arbitrary devmgr commands
with the consequences of that command; the SSH aliases do not restrict the command set.

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or id from list_local_sites; for example "Default".

action.description:
build, sdp_answer, close or a devmgr command name; for example
"build".

params.description:
Further body keys sent as given; for example
{"mac": "02:00:5e:00:53:01"}. Free-form object.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: manage_esim_profile
tools.description:
Add or delete an eSIM profile on a UniFi mobile-broadband device.

Required: host, site, action and params. action add sends Classic POST
api/s/{site}/cmd/mbb with cmd esim-add; action delete sends cmd esim-delete. The
Network 11.0.81 web app builds the rest of the body dynamically, so params is
free-form and sent as given beside cmd. eSIM activation codes in it are masked in
errors and results only under UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS. Returns the
Classic envelope {meta, data} verbatim; success requires meta.rc "ok". With
dry-run policy returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: delete erases the eSIM profile from the device; a carrier profile
usually cannot be downloaded again without a new activation code.

"version"}, both sent as given. Consequence: changes the controller's firmware
cache; no device is upgraded.

Success is HTTP 2xx with meta.rc "ok"; anything else raises with the full upstream body.
Returns the upstream body verbatim.

Under dry-run policy nothing is sent and the tool returns a dry-run preview: status
"dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message and preview (method, path, params, body). Never
auto-retried.

tools.name: manage_mclag_group
tools.description:
Create, update or delete an MC-LAG switch group (Network v2 route).

Consequence: changes switch link aggregation; links can drop. action "create": POST
/proxy/network/v2/api/site/{site}/mclag-groups with group verbatim. action "update": reads
GET .../mclag-groups, merges only the given leaves, PUT .../mclag-groups/{id} with the
merged record and reads it back, adding _verified (type-strict per requested leaf) and
_readAfterError. action "delete": DELETE .../mclag-groups/{id} (irreversible). Update and
delete resolve group_id in the list first (an unknown id fails listing every valid id).
group is required for create and update and omitted for delete; group_id is required for
update and delete and omitted for create. Returns the upstream body (JSON object or
array) verbatim for actions "create" and "update"; for action "update" a non-object
body is returned whole under response with _verified (and _readAfterError) beside it.
Action "delete" returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is true, message
summarizes the delete, and response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON, raw
text, or null when the body is empty).
Never auto-retried.

Under dry-run policy nothing is sent and the tool returns a dry-run preview:
status "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message and preview (method, path, params, body); for
action "delete" that preview is the response of {status: "dry_run", deleted: false, message,
response}.

tools.name: query_traffic_flows
tools.description:
Query traffic flows: a Network v2 read-POST, available in read-only and dry-run modes.

POST /proxy/network/v2/api/site/{site}/traffic-flows. Allowlisted by live read
evidence (2026-10-26, 50+ calls, configuration digests unchanged); dry-run policy
sends it normally. Body keys override typed selectors. Window becomes epoch-ms
timestampFrom/timestampTo; direction, action and risk become lists.

Without pageSize, drain every page reported by has_next/total_page_count from
pageNumber (default 0). A body pageSize above 5000 is sent as 5000 per page
(larger wire sizes cause HTTP 400); at or below 5000 it is sent as given.
Every integer pageSize requests that many records or fewer at the end, starting
at pageNumber * pageSize. Upstream errors pass through unchanged. No time-window
or page-count cap applies, including UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES; large queries can
consume substantial controller memory and time.

_nextPage {offset, pageSize} resumes at the first unreturned record: pass the
object as body.pageNumber, with any new body.pageSize or omit to reuse its size.
_pageSize {requested, sent, effective, returned} reports each physical request
size in sent, the observed console size in effective, and the returned count.

Returns a single-page result verbatim, or for several pages (with or without
pageSize) the last page's envelope with gathered data and _pages. Repeated/empty
pages claiming more return gathered data with incomplete and incompleteReason; a
later failure also names its zero-based page, status and full upstream error.

Required arguments: host, site.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

site.description: Required Network site name or UUID from list_local_sites, e.g. "Default".

body.description:
Optional free-form query body; its keys take precedence over selectors.
Explicit timestamps use epoch ms, e.g. {"timestampFrom": 1710000000000}.

window.description: Duration converted to epoch-millisecond bounds, e.g. "5m".

direction.description:
Shape: string|string[]; sent as an array.
Observed values local, outgoing, incoming (2026-10-26).
Any value is forwarded for the console to validate, e.g. "outgoing".

action.description:
Shape: string|string[]; sent as an array.
Observed values allowed, blocked (2026-10-26).
Any value is forwarded for the console to validate, e.g. "blocked".

risk.description:
Shape: string|string[]; sent as an array.
Observed values low, medium, high (2026-10-26).
Any value is forwarded for the console to validate, e.g. "high".

tools.name: set_client_fingerprint_override
tools.description:
Override (or restore) the device type the controller detected for a client.

Consequence: the controller reports the overridden device type for the client in

{dev_id_override: fingerprint device id, mac, plus optional search_query, dev_type,
dev_vendor, dev_model}; mac is added from the client when the body has none. Returns the
upstream body of that PUT verbatim. override omitted: DELETE on the same route restores
automatic detection and returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is true, message
summarizes the delete, and response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON, raw
text, or null when the body is empty). The current state is fingerprint.has_override /
dev_id_override in list_dhcp_leases or get_local_client. Route: v2 only (no official
route).

Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: a PUT returns the dry-run preview unchanged; a DELETE
(restore detection) returns {status: "dry_run", deleted: false, message, response}
with the preview as response.

The PUT dry-run preview is {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params, body}}.

Example call (set_client_fingerprint_override):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "client": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff",
     "override": {"dev_id_override": 4}}

Set or remove the custom (AI-generated) icon of a client or a Matter node.

Consequence: changes only the icon the controller UI shows for that client or node
(removal restores the default icon); connectivity is unaffected.

Icon given: PUT v2 clients/{mac}/ai-icon (or matter/nodes/{id}/ai-icon) with the icon object
as the body. Returns the upstream body of that PUT verbatim. icon omitted: DELETE on the
same route restores the default icon and returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is
true, message summarizes the delete, and response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded
JSON, raw text, or null when the body is empty). Route: v2 only (no official route).
Request body: no published schema; the web app sends its icon generator's object
{icon_id, icon_set_id, request_id, selected_index, assets: [{url, width, height}]} as
the body; an empty body answers HTTP 400
"Validation failure". A MAC that is neither a connected client nor a known client
(stat/alluser) is refused before any request, listing the valid clients; the upstream
answers HTTP 404 api.err.ClientNotFound only for a known MAC with no v2 client record.

body) is returned unchanged for a PUT; a DELETE (icon removal) returns {status: "dry_run",
deleted: false, message, response} with the preview as response.

{method, path, params, body}}.

Client MAC (any form) or connected client UUID; for target_type

Free-form icon object to set; omit to restore the default icon, e.g.

request_id, selected_index and assets ([{url, width, height}]).

tools.name: set_lte_apn_profile

connectivity until it is corrected.

body that is not a JSON object arrives as {result: ...}. The
password is a credential: UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS masks it. With dry-run policy,
returns {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path,
params, body}} and sends nothing.

Required inputs: host, action, console_mac.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

ups_mac.description: MAC of the UPS to pair with (pair); for example "02:00:5e:00:53:02".

username.description:
UI account username or email for the UPS (pair); for example

Console name or id: the short name from list_hosts
(data[].reportedState.hostname or reportedState.name, case-insensitive,

/proxy/network/v2/api/site/{site}/content-filtering/{_id} and reads it back: the

the read-back failed. An empty update is refused before any request.

read back equal, type-strict) and _readAfterError when the read-back failed; a
non-object PUT body is kept under response.

tools.name: update_setting
tools.description:
Update a controller setting group by key.

Discover the schema first by calling get_setting(setting_key): it returns every
settable field and its current (valid) value. The controller silently drops any
unrecognised field or enum value (HTTP 200, value unchanged), so a guessed value
fails invisibly; this tool reports that no-op separately from the PUT response, naming
every rejected field and pointing you back at get_setting. The check walks the payload
leaf by leaf: a nested object is compared as a partial update (only the keys you send
must take), and a
nested leaf left unchanged is named by its dotted path (e.g. radius.port) even when a sibling
leaf in the same object was applied; _verificationNote names the rejected and applied
leaves.

Returns: the controller's PUT response envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [setting group]} verbatim
plus the additive _verified: true only when the read-after confirms every submitted leaf
(type-strict: true is not 1), false with _unverifiedFields (dotted paths) when a leaf was
rejected or changed to a value other than the one sent (v0.6.2 raised for a rejected
leaf; check _verified), null with _readAfterError when the read-after failed or could not
be matched (the write was still sent). When every submitted field already holds the sent
value, no PUT is made and the current GET envelope is returned verbatim plus an additive
_note "no change needed".
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status: "dry_run",
dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

Request body: no published schema exists for PUT network/api/s/{site}/rest/setting/{setting_key}
(classic controller API). Pass the controller's native payload; read the current object first
with the matching list/get tool and send back the edited object.

    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "setting_key": "mgmt",
      "payload": {"led_enabled": false}
    }

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, {meta: {rc}, data: [the updated group]}.
Additive _warnings (NO_ID_RETURNED, NOT_STORED_AS_SENT: field names only) report a
write that did not land as sent. Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the bare dry-run
preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path,
params, body}}.

Example call (update_user_group):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "group_id": "000000000000000000000101",
     "group": {"qos_rate_max_down": 20000}}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

group_id.description: User group _id from list_user_groups (data[]._id).

group.description:
Native usergroup fields to change, e.g. name, qos_rate_max_down,
qos_rate_max_up. Free-form JSON object; no published body shape.

tools.name: update_wan_interface
tools.description:
Update a WAN interface configuration.

A WAN interface is a Classic REST networkconf record of purpose wan, written with PUT
/proxy/network/api/s/{site}/rest/networkconf/{_id} (the route the controller's own UI uses;
the published Integration API serves WANs GET-only, PUT answers HTTP 404 "No endpoint" on
Network 11.0.81). The id is resolved among the site's wan records first; an unknown id fails
listing every WAN with both ids. Send only the fields to change: the Classic PUT merges them
into the stored record.

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, the Classic envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [the updated
networkconf record]}.
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status: "dry_run",
dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

Example call (update_wan_interface):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "wan_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
      "wan": {"wan_load_balance_weight": 50}
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

wan_id.description:
WAN interface id. Get it from list_wan_interfaces (data[].id); the Classic
networkconf _id also works. Network-app UUID — not a Protect id.

wan.description:
Native Classic networkconf fields to change, e.g. name, wan_type, wan_dns1,
wan_load_balance_weight, wan_failover_priority, wan_vlan_enabled. Sent unchanged
(empty-string list placeholders dropped); an absent or null purpose is sent as
wan, another is sent as given (an upstream error then gets a hint).
A purpose-only update is refused.
Free-form JSON object; no fixed body shape is published.

tools.name: update_wan_load_balancing
tools.description:
Change the site's multi-WAN load-balancing configuration and verify it.

Required: host, site and configuration (the fields to change). Reads the current
configuration (GET /v2/api/site/{site}/wan/load-balancing/configuration), merges
configuration over it (objects merge, other values replace) and PUTs the result,
then reads it back. Returns the PUT response verbatim (a non-object response under
response) plus _verified (true, false, or null when the read-back failed),
_unverifiedFields when false, _readAfterError and _redactedFieldsNotSent (with
UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS on, the fields that held the redaction mask, left out of the PUT).
An empty configuration is refused before any request. With dry-run policy returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent:
false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: WAN traffic is redistributed across the gateway's uplinks at once.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or id from list_local_sites; for example "Default".

configuration.description: Fields to change, free-form; for example {"mode": "failover"}.

test_config_id.description:
Sent as the testConfigId query parameter; for example
"example-test-config".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: update_wan_sla
tools.description:
Change a WAN SLA definition and verify it.

Required: host, site, sla_id (an _id from list_wan_slas; an unknown id fails
listing them) and changes. Reads the SLA from GET /v2/api/site/{site}/wan-slas,
merges changes over it, PUTs the result to .../wan-slas/{_id} (its _id and id in
the upstream spelling) and reads the list back. Returns the PUT response verbatim
(a non-object response under response) plus _verified (true, false, or null when
the read-back failed), _unverifiedFields when false, _readAfterError and
_redactedFieldsNotSent (with UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS on, the fields that held the
redaction mask, left out of the PUT). An empty changes
object is refused before any request. With dry-run policy returns a dry-run preview
{status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} and
sends nothing.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or id from list_local_sites; for example "Default".

changes.description: Fields to change; for example {"name": "Branch SLA"}. Free-form object.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: update_wifi_broadcast
tools.description:
Update an existing WiFi broadcast SSID.

Returns the upstream response body verbatim: the updated WiFi broadcast object the API
answers
with (under dry-run policy, the dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params (query parameters), body}} instead).


For an open SSID use securityConfiguration: {type: "OPEN"} and an explicit network
reference: network: {type: "SPECIFIC", networkId: UUID from list_networks}. Retain that
reference in the full replacement object; the live controller requires it for OPEN.

Full request shapes are in the parameter schema; detailed examples and workflows:
docs/TOOL-USAGE.md#update_wifi_broadcast.

Required arguments: host, site, broadcast_id, broadcast (see parameter descriptions for
identifiers).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

broadcast_id.description:
WiFi broadcast (SSID) UUID. Get it from list_wifi_broadcasts (data[].id).
Network-app UUID — not a Protect id.

broadcast.description:
FULL replacement object (PUT; omitted fields reset); spec Wifi broadcast create
or update. 'type' selects variant: IOT_OPTIMIZED|STANDARD.
Advisory spec fields; any JSON passes. Required: channel2gLockedTo6, clientIsolationEnabled, dtimPeriod2gLockedTo3, enabled, hideName, multicastToUnicastConversionEnabled, name, securityConfiguration, type, uapsdEnabled. Variants by type: IOT_OPTIMIZED; STANDARD (requires advertiseDeviceName, arpProxyEnabled, broadcastingFrequenciesGHz, bssTransitionEnabled; optional bandSteeringEnabled, dnsAssistanceConfiguration, dtimPeriodByFrequencyGHzOverride, handoffSuggestionsConfiguration, hotspotConfiguration, mloEnabled).
For OPEN securityConfiguration, supply an explicit network reference: network: {type: "SPECIFIC", networkId: UUID from list_networks}. The live controller requires it although the spec marks network optional.

advertiseDeviceName.description: Indicates whether the device name is advertised in beacon frames.

arpProxyEnabled.description: Whether the access point answers ARP for clients.

bandSteeringEnabled.description: Whether capable clients are steered to 5 GHz.

broadcastingDeviceFilter.description: Defines the custom scope of devices that will broadcast this WiFi network. Shape: {type:'DEVICES',deviceIds:string(uuid)[]}|{type:'DEVICE_TAGS',deviceTagIds:string(uuid)[]}

channel2gLockedTo6.description: Locks 2.4GHz radio channel to 6 on all broadcasting devices

clientIsolationEnabled.description: Whether clients are isolated from each other.

dtimPeriod2gLockedTo3.description: Locks DTIM period to 3 for 2.4GHz radio

handoffSuggestionsConfiguration.description: Suggests low-signal clients to roam to a better access point. Shape: {band5GHzRssiThreshold?:integer,band6GHzRssiThreshold?:integer}

mloEnabled.description: Whether WiFi 7 Multi-Link Operation is enabled.

multicastToUnicastConversionEnabled.description: Whether multicast is converted to unicast.

type.description: Variant tag; one of: 'IOT_OPTIMIZED', 'STANDARD'.

uapsdEnabled.description: Indicates whether Unscheduled Automatic Power Save Delivery (U-APSD) is enabled

tools.name: update_wlan_config
tools.description:
Update a WLAN (SSID) configuration by ID.

The id is resolved in list_wlan_configs first: an unknown id fails listing every valid _id, and
nothing is written.

Returns: the controller's Classic REST response envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [...]}
verbatim (meta is relayed as received, never interpreted).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status: "dry_run",
dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

Request body: no published schema exists for PUT network/api/s/{site}/rest/wlanconf/{id}
(classic/v2 controller API). Pass the controller's native payload; read the current object first
with the matching list/get tool and send back the edited object.

Example call (update_wlan_config):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "wlan_id": "000000000000000000000107",
      "payload": {"enabled": false}
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

wlan_id.description:
Classic WLAN config _id (wlanconf). Get it from list_wlan_configs (_id). Not a wifi
broadcast UUID.

payload.description:
spec: free-form (classic REST wlanconf). Fields to change, e.g. x_passphrase,
security, enabled. Read current via get_wlan_config.
Free-form JSON object; no fixed body shape is published.

tools.name: verify_sim_pin
tools.description:
Unlock a PIN-locked SIM card by sending its PIN.

Required: host, site and pin. manager lte (default) sends Classic POST
api/s/{site}/cmd/lte with cmd lte-verify-pin and {mac, pin}, the keys the Network
11.0.81 web app sends; manager mbb sends cmd/mbb with cmd verify-pin, whose other
keys the web app builds dynamically: pass them in params (free-form, sent as
given; a pin key, or a mac key together with the mac argument, fails before any
request). mac, when given, must be a device of the site (from list_devices). Returns
the Classic envelope {meta, data} verbatim; success requires meta.rc "ok". The PIN
is a credential: masked in errors and results only under
UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS. With dry-run policy returns a dry-run preview
{status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} and
sends nothing.

Consequence: each wrong PIN uses one of the SIM's few attempts; the last one locks
the SIM until its PUK is entered.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home UDM") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or id from list_local_sites; for example "Default".

params.description: Free-form extra command fields; for example {"slot": 1}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: accept_ironclad_terms
tools.description:
Record acceptance of a Protect service agreement.

POST protect/api/ironclad/sendAcceptance with {"cid", "vid", "status", "type"},
where type is agreement_type. Returns: the upstream response unchanged.

Consequence: a legal acceptance of that agreement version is recorded upstream; it
cannot be withdrawn through this tool.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host, cid, vid, status, agreement_type.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

cid.description: Agreement contract id as Protect supplies it, e.g. "contract-1".

vid.description: Agreement version id as Protect supplies it, e.g. "version-3".

status.description: Acceptance status sent as status, e.g. "accepted".

agreement_type.description: Agreement type sent as type, e.g. "cloud-archive".

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: add_protect_case_asset
tools.description:
Add a recording clip from one camera to a Protect case.

Consequence: the clip is attached to the case for everyone with access to it; the
recording itself is unchanged.

Sends {camera, type, start, end, note?, lens?, ...fields} to POST
/cases/{case_id}/assets, start and end converted from epoch SECONDS to ms. To add
an event, pass its camera and start/end (event times are ms; divide by 1000).
Returns {status: "created", response: {main: {success, data: ASSET}}}. The
console accepts asset_type "clip" only (live-probed). With dry-run policy, returns
{status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, case_id, camera_id, start, end.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

case_id.description: Case id from list_protect_cases; for example "000000000000000000000c01".

camera_id.description: Camera id (an event's camera field); for example "000000000000000000000103".

start.description: Clip start, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760227200.

end.description: Clip end, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760227230.

note.description: Note shown on the asset; for example "Person at side door".

lens.description:
Lenses of a package-camera doorbell, "main" and/or "secondary"; for
example ["main"].
Shape: ('main'|'secondary')[]

fields.description:
Other asset fields sent as given (free-form object); for example
{"title": "Side door"}.
A key a typed argument also sets fails before any request.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: adopt_protect_device
tools.description:
Adopt an available Protect device using its native id. Adoption changes management and
may interrupt service. Returns the relay status and unchanged upstream adoption result;
no automatic retry. An unknown id may return a per-device error in an HTTP 200 response.

Consequence: this console's Protect application takes over management of the device, which
is provisioned and may restart (briefly interrupting its stream). Adoption persists until
the device is removed with unadopt_protect_device.

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.
Write metadata includes writeEnabled; _warnings describes operational risks.

Under dry-run policy no upstream write is sent: status is "dry_run" and body
contains the exact preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params (query parameters), body}}.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number or dry_run for a preview.

Example call (adopt_protect_device):
    {"host": "my-console", "device_type": "camera", "device_id": "00000000000000000000010b"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

device_type.description:
Protect resource kind, singular: "camera" or "sensor" (the route
adds the plural collection, e.g. protect/api/cameras).

device_id.description:
Protect device id (24-hex) from list_cameras / list_sensors (id),
e.g. "00000000000000000000010b", or an unambiguous device name such as
"Front Door".

tools.name: adopt_third_party_camera
tools.description:
Adopt a third-party (ONVIF) camera into Protect.

Consequence: the camera is added to the console and starts recording under its
recording settings; it uses a camera licence slot where one is required.

Sends camera as the body of POST /third-party-cameras/adopt on the private Protect
API (no official route). The web UI builds the body at run time, so it is sent as
given (free-form object), usually the camera address and its login. The camera
password is a registered credential: it is masked in previews, results and error
text only when UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS is on, and always scrubbed from logs. Sent once.
Returns {status: "adopt_requested", response} with the upstream body verbatim.
With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW}. Dry-run
response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, camera (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

camera.description:
Adoption body sent as given (free-form object); for example
{"host": "192.0.2.50", "username": "admin", "password": "example-pass"}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: alarm_hub_trigger_output
tools.description:
Trigger an alarm-hub output (POST /v1/alarm-hubs/{id}/outputs/{outputId}/trigger).

Consequence: whatever is wired to the output (siren, strobe, lock, relay) acts in the real
world.

Returns {status: "sent", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON,
the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

WARNING: physically triggers alarm-hub output hardware. `enable` true turns the
output on, false off (omit to toggle); `delay` is ms before activating; `duration` is
ms to stay active (0 = indefinite). Governed by family:protect=deny.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/alarm-hubs/{id}/outputs/{outputId}/trigger; schema
"inline requestBody schema") is built from scalar parameters. No key is required; send only the
keys to change.
- enable: boolean
- delay: integer (ms)
- duration: integer (ms; 0 = indefinite)

Example call (alarm_hub_trigger_output):
    {"host": "my-console", "alarm_hub_id": "00000000000000000000010b", "output_id": 0}

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

alarm_hub_id.description:
Protect alarm hub id. Get it from list_alarm_hubs (id). Protect id (24-hex) —
not a Network device UUID.

output_id.description:
Output channel id on that device; spec: integer 0 or 1 (an integer, or the same
value as a decimal string '0'|'1'). See get_alarm_hub.

confirm.description: Ignored. The call runs when made; there is no confirmation step.

enable.description: true = on, false = off; omit to toggle.

tools.name: analyze_footage_with_ai
tools.description:
Ask the console's AI processor to describe a camera's footage in words.

Consequence: runs a vision-language analysis on the console's AI processor
(compute load); nothing is changed on the camera.

Sends {cameraId, channel?, eventId?, timestamp?} to POST /aiprocessors/vlm/analyze
on the private Protect API (no official route); only the arguments you pass are
sent. timestamp is epoch SECONDS and is sent as milliseconds. A POST, so it counts
as a write (read-only mode refuses it). Returns {status: "sent", response} with the
analysis verbatim. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response:
PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, camera_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

camera_id.description:
Camera id (24-hex) from list_cameras; for example
"00000000000000000000010b".

timestamp.description: Moment to analyze, epoch SECONDS (sent as ms); for example 1760227200.

channel.description: Camera channel index (0 is the highest quality); for example 0.

event_id.description: Event id from list_protect_events; for example "000000000000000000000e01".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: apply_recognized_image
tools.description:
Apply the result of a recognize_image run to Protect's recognition data.

POST protect/api/recognition/recognize-image/apply (private Protect API) with
apply as the JSON body; the upstream response is returned unchanged. The
frontend builds this body dynamically and the key set is not documented, so no
key is required here and the upstream judges it. Build it from the answer of
recognize_image. Fields are sent as given except: keys starting with "_" and
values the server masks as redacted are dropped (reported on the result), and a
body left with no field to send (empty, or only empty objects) is refused
before any request with "No fields provided" (the message
reads "apply 'settings'"). Nothing else is added, removed or rewritten. Under
dry-run policy it returns a dry-run preview. Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and
family:protect=deny.
Consequence: the console stores the recognition outcome of the uploaded image
(for example adding it to a recognition group).
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null); under
dry-run policy the preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params, body}}.

Required arguments: host, apply.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

apply.description:
Free-form JSON object built from the recognize_image response; its
keys are not documented, so none are prescribed here. Sent as given
apart from the dropped fields described above,
e.g. `{"recognize_image response key": "value"}`.

tools.name: assign_detections_to_recognition_group
tools.description:
Assign recognition detections to a recognition group.

POST protect/api/recognition/{type}/assign-group with the body the Protect web app
sends, {"objectIds": detection_ids, "groupId": group_id}; the upstream response is
returned unchanged. An empty or non-list detection_ids, or an empty group_id, is
refused before any request. Under dry-run policy it returns a dry-run preview.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny.
Consequence: the detections move out of the group that held them and are
re-labelled as the target group on the console.
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null); under
dry-run policy the preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params, body}}.

Required arguments: host, type.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

type.description: Use "face" or "vehicle" (singular; plural forms return HTTP 400 upstream).

detection_ids.description:
Shape: string[]. Ids of the detections to move, from
list_recognition_detections, e.g. ["000000000000000000000116"].

group_id.description:
Id of the group that receives them, from list_recognition_groups,
e.g. "face_90".

assignment.description:
Legacy native body sent verbatim when supplied instead of the typed
arguments; it takes precedence, so detection_ids and group_id are then ignored.
Free-form object. Shape: {objectIds:string[],groupId:string}.

tools.name: assign_sensor_to_bridge
tools.description:
Assign a Protect sensor to a specific bridge for its wireless connection.

Consequence: the sensor reconnects through the named bridge; it can be briefly
offline while it moves.

Sends {assignedBridge: bridge_id} to POST /sensors/{sensor_id}/assign-bridge on the
private Protect API (no official route). Sent once. Returns {status: "assigned",
response} with the upstream body verbatim. With dry-run policy, returns {status:
"dry_run", response: PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, sensor_id, bridge_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

sensor_id.description:
Sensor id (24-hex) from list_sensors; for example
"00000000000000000000010d".

bridge_id.description:
Bridge id (24-hex) from list_bridges, sent as assignedBridge; for
example "00000000000000000000010e".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: bulk_upload_vehicle_groups
tools.description:
Create vehicle recognition groups in bulk from a filled-in upload file.

Sends the decoded file (the template from get_vehicle_group_upload_template, filled
in) as a multipart file part with POST
protect/api/recognition/vehicle/groups/batch-upload; the upstream response is
returned unchanged. Invalid base64 is refused before any request. Under
dry-run policy it returns a dry-run preview (part name, filename, type and size).
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny.
Consequence: every vehicle row in the file is created as a recognition group.
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null), a binary
answer as {image_base64, content_type, size_bytes}; under dry-run policy the
preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params,
body}}.

Required arguments: host, filename, file_content_base64.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

filename.description: File name sent with the part, e.g. "vehicles.csv".

content_type.description:
Part MIME type, e.g. "text/csv". Required when the filename
extension is not an image or audio type.

form_field.description:
Multipart field name, default "file" (the published Protect
upload's name), e.g. "file".

tools.name: calibrate_camera
tools.description:
Start a camera calibration (PTZ / motorised lens), as the Protect web app does.

Sends POST cameras/{camera_id}/calibrate (no body) once on the Protect console host,
never auto-retried on 429. Returns {status: "sent", response} with the console's
answer verbatim; a camera without calibration answers with its error. With
dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Consequence: the camera moves through its full range while it calibrates, so its
view is interrupted until calibration ends.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: calibrate_door_lock
tools.description:
Run the calibration routine of a UniFi door lock.

Consequence: the lock motor drives the bolt through its travel, so the door is
unlocked and locked during calibration; keep the door closed and clear.

Sends POST /doorlocks/{doorlock_id}/calibrate on the private Protect API (no
official route). The web UI builds the body at run time, so options is sent as

tools.name: clear_sensor_tamper

response; _readAfter reports current sensor state without claiming success from HTTP
alone. Failed read-back preserves the response with readAfterError and null
_verified/_noOp verdicts. No automatic retry.

no longer shows as tampered; the cleared flag cannot be restored, but a new tamper event
latches it again. Nothing happens physically at the sensor.

body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.
Write metadata includes writeEnabled; _warnings describes operational risks.

Under dry-run policy no upstream write is sent: status is "dry_run" and body
contains the exact preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params (query parameters), body}}.

tools.name: collect_protect_device_changes
tools.description:
Collect Protect device add/remove/modify changes by polling every device family for
poll_count complete snapshots. The WebSocket subscription is unavailable through Fabric;
this read-only, stateless tool is its REST equivalent.

Returns {_poll_count, _polls, _truncated, changes}; each change has
change=added|removed|modified and the upstream device object verbatim (current for
added/modified, last-seen for removed). Heartbeat-only lastSeen/uptime/upSince changes are
ignored. Objects without id cannot be diffed: each distinct object appears verbatim in
unidentified as {family, device}, even if later absent; heartbeat-only differences collapse
to the latest form. These produce incomplete/incompleteReason.

404/501 families appear in unavailableFamilies with their complete upstream errors and
incomplete=true. A family unavailable in either consecutive poll is excluded from that diff,
preventing false additions/removals. Every family unavailable raises the upstream error. A
failed first poll raises; failure after a successful poll stops and returns collected
changes with incomplete=true and the complete poll error in incompleteReason. Other families
still count. Full workflow: docs/TOOL-USAGE.md#collect_protect_device_changes.

Required arguments: host (see parameter descriptions for identifiers).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

poll_count.description:
positive integer number of complete snapshots (default 6). At least two
polls detect changes; elapsed time never interrupts an active snapshot.

max_changes.description:
Optional early stop: once this many change records accumulate, stop and flag
`_truncated=true`. Default None (omit it): no limit, all requested polls complete.

poll_interval_seconds.description:
pacing delay between completed polls (default 2). This never
bounds request duration or cancels active work.
Zero means no timed delay; the event loop still yields. Small values may hit
the shared 429 backoff, which the client handles.

tools.name: collect_protect_events
tools.description:
Collect Protect events over a bounded polling window (live-feed stand-in).

The window is bounded by `poll_count` complete polls, never by elapsed time.
The result adds incomplete / incompleteReason when a poll's drain stopped short or a
later poll failed.

Protect's `/v1/subscribe/events` WebSocket feed is NOT reachable over the Fabric
cloud connector (a unary request/response relay — verified: an upgrade GET
returns 404, never 101). This tool is the REST equivalent: it polls the
historical-events path for `poll_count` complete polls and returns every distinct event
seen in one call. Read-only and stateless — each call starts fresh and holds no
cursor between calls.

Returns {result, _poll_count, _polls, _truncated} — result holds the verbatim upstream
objects, de-duplicated by event id with the LATEST object per id kept; an event with no
id is de-duplicated by its full record (an identical id-less event seen by several
polls is kept, and counted toward max_events, once). Each poll
drains every page; there is no page cap by default, and only the opt-in
UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES can stop a poll early (the result then carries incomplete:
true with the reason). When a poll fails after an earlier poll succeeded (any error: an
HTTP error, a 429 that outlasted the retries, a transport or shape error), polling stops
and the events gathered so far are returned with incomplete: true and an
incompleteReason carrying that poll's complete error; a failing first poll raises it.
An upstream 404/501 (Protect absent) is passed straight through.

Required arguments: host (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

poll_count.description:
positive integer number of complete polls in the bounded polling window
(default 6). An active poll is never interrupted by elapsed time; lifecycle
cancellation remains available.

max_events.description:
Optional early stop: once this many distinct events are collected, stop and
flag `_truncated=true`. Default None (omit it): no limit, all requested polls complete.
A single poll is never truncated mid-page, so the count may slightly exceed it.

since.description:
optional epoch SECONDS lower bound; defaults to the moment the call starts, so only
events at/after the call are collected. A negative or millisecond-magnitude value
(>= 1e11) is not refused: it is converted to milliseconds like any time, and the result
carries a _warnings entry.

smart_detect_types.description:
same filters and validation as `list_protect_events` (camera names
resolve to IDs; smart_detect_types without types is sent with a _warnings entry).
Shape: string|string[]

poll_interval_seconds.description:
pacing delay between completed polls (default 2). This never
bounds request duration or cancels active work.
Zero means no timed delay; the event loop still yields. Small values may hit
the shared 429 backoff, which the client handles.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort order sent on every poll as orderDirection: "ASC"
(oldest-first) or "DESC" (newest-first). Omitted (default): no orderDirection is sent
and the upstream's own order applies.

tools.name: create_arm_profile
tools.description:

Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/arm-profiles; schema "inline requestBody schema") is
passed in `name` + settings (merged; settings must NOT contain name). Required keys — name,
automations, schedules, recordEverything, activationDelay.
- name: string 1-255
- automations: array of string (automation ids)
- schedules: array of armSchedule objects {start: string (cron expression), end: string
  (cron expression)} (both required)
- recordEverything: boolean
- activationDelay: one of 0|60000|300000|600000 (ms)

Example call (create_arm_profile):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "name": "Night",
      "settings": {
        "automations": [],
        "schedules": [],
        "recordEverything": false,
        "activationDelay": 0
      }
    }

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

name.description:
REQUIRED profile name (1-255 chars), sent as the body field name. Do not repeat it
inside settings; a settings['name'] that differs from this value is rejected with a
clear error.

settings.description:
Rest of the body (Protect 7.3.74 POST /v1/arm-profiles). Required: automations,
schedules, recordEverything, activationDelay (0|60000|300000|600000). Leave name out; it
comes from the name argument.
Advisory spec fields; any JSON passes. Required: activationDelay, automations, name, recordEverything, schedules.

automations.description: List of automation IDs associated with this arm profile. Shape: string[]

recordEverything.description: Whether to record everything when this arm profile is active.

One shortcut object, sent inside an array (free-form); for example
{"placement": {"x": 0, "y": 0}, "shortcut": {"type": "webhook", "name":
"Gate view", "url": "http://192.0.2.1/", "method": "GET", "headers": null,
"body": null, "auth": null, "timeout": 1}}.

tools.name: create_liveview
tools.description:
Create a liveview on a Protect console.

Returns {status: "created", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON,
the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/liveviews; schema "inline requestBody schema") is passed
in `settings`. Required keys — id, modelKey, name, isDefault, isGlobal, owner, layout, slots.
- id: string
- modelKey: string
- name: string
- isDefault: boolean
- isGlobal: boolean
- owner: string
- layout: number (1-26; the number of slots)
- slots: array of object {cameras: array of string (camera ids), cycleMode:
  enum[motion|time], cycleInterval: number (seconds)} (every item key required)
Spec POST /v1/liveviews body is allOf[liveview] whose required list includes server-side fields
(id, modelKey, owner); tool merges name + settings into the body. Provide layout + slots; treat
id/modelKey/owner requirement as spec-as-published.

Example call (create_liveview):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "name": "Front of house",
      "settings": {
        "id": "00000000000000000000010b",
        "modelKey": "liveview",
        "isDefault": true,
        "isGlobal": true,
        "owner": "00000000000000000000010b",
        "layout": 9,
        "slots": [
          {
            "cameras": ["00000000000000000000010b"],
            "cycleMode": "motion",
            "cycleInterval": 10
          }
        ]
      }
    }

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

isDefault.description: Whether this live view is the default one for all viewers.

isGlobal.description: Whether this live view is global and available system-wide to all users

layout.description: The number of slots this live view contains.

modelKey.description: The model key of the liveview

name.description: The name of this live view.

slots.description: List of cameras visible in each given slot. Shape: ({cameras:string[],cycleInterval:number,cycleMode:'motion'|'time'})[]

settings.description:
Rest of the body (Protect 7.3.74 POST /v1/liveviews), merged with name. Provide
layout, slots, id, modelKey, isDefault, isGlobal and owner, all required by the
published schema. Leave name out; it comes from the name argument.
Shape: {layout:number,slots:{cameras:string[],cycleMode:'motion'|'time',
cycleInterval:number}[],id:string,modelKey:string,isDefault:boolean,
isGlobal:boolean,owner:string}
Advisory spec fields; any JSON passes. Required: id, isDefault, isGlobal, layout, modelKey, name, owner, slots.

Returns {status: "created", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON,
the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

`qualities`: list of channel names to enable. The exhaustive set is 'high', 'medium',
  'low', and 'package' (verified live against get_rtsps_stream, which reports exactly
  these four channel keys). 'package' exists only on package-camera doorbells; on other
  cameras it is null. There is NO 'highest' channel. Each value must be exactly one of
  those spec enum values (lowercase); any other value, a different case included, fails
  before any request.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/cameras/{id}/rtsps-stream; schema "inline requestBody
schema") is built from scalar parameters. Required keys — qualities.
- qualities: array of enum high|medium|low|package

Example call (create_rtsps_stream):
    {"host": "my-console", "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b", "qualities": ["high"]}

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id. Get it from list_cameras (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a
Network device UUID.

qualities.description:
Channels to enable (at least one; an empty list fails before any request,
spec minItems 1); spec enum channelQuality: high|medium|low|package (package only on
cameras with a package lens).

response (the preview)}.

Protect camera id. Get it from list_cameras (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a

Channel to delete ('high'), or a list of channels (at least one; an empty list

tools.name: enroll_doorbell_credential
tools.description:
Enroll an NFC card or fingerprint on a doorbell (G4/G6 Pro class) for a user.

The credential_type is nfc or fingerprint. step enroll (POST cameras/{camera_id}/
{credential_type}/enroll) puts the doorbell on the Protect console host into enrollment
mode; present the card or finger. step assign (POST .../{credential_type}/assign) assigns
the read credential to a user: the body is fields plus fingerprintId and ulpId when given
(the bundle's fingerprint keys; the NFC body is not published, pass its keys in fields).
step cancel (POST .../{credential_type}/cancel) leaves enrollment mode. fingerprint_id,
ulp_id and fields apply to step assign only; giving any of them with another step fails
before any request. Returns {status, response}: status: "enrolling" for step enroll,
status: "assigned" for assign and status: "cancelled" for cancel. Credential
identifiers are registered secrets, masked only under UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS. With
dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Consequence: an assigned card or fingerprint can unlock or identify the user at the
doorbell until it is deleted with delete_doorbell_credential.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description:
Doorbell camera id from list_cameras; for example
"000000000000000000000103".

step.description: enroll, assign or cancel; for example "enroll".

fingerprint_id.description:
assign only: the read fingerprint id, sent as fingerprintId;
for example "3".

ulp_id.description:
assign only: the UniFi user id, sent as ulpId (list_ulp_users); for
example "0f6a1c2e-3b4d-4e5f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b".

fields.description:
assign only: other body keys sent as given (free-form); for example
{"name": "Front door card"}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: export_camera_video
tools.description:
Export an MP4 clip or timelapse through the private video route. Returns the entire
uncapped payload base64-encoded in bodyBase64 with sizeBytes and contentType; body is
null for binary output. Base64 expands bytes by about one third and the whole response
occupies memory, so long clips can produce very large MCP messages. Requested clip
boundaries may differ by a few seconds. Set fps for a timelapse; no duration or payload
cap is imposed.
The additive ``_warnings`` entry flags negative or millisecond-looking epoch inputs while
sending values as given.

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number.

Example call (export_camera_video):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b",
      "start": 1735689600,
      "end": 1735689610
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id (24-hex) from list_cameras (id), e.g.
"00000000000000000000010b", or an unambiguous camera name such as "Front Door".

start.description:
Clip start in epoch seconds, e.g. 1735689600; converted to controller
milliseconds.

end.description:
Clip end in epoch seconds, e.g. 1735689610; converted to controller
milliseconds.

channel.description:
Stream index, e.g. 0 for high quality; index 3 selects package-camera lens
2.

fps.description:
Optional timelapse frame rate, e.g. 4 for 60x or 8 for 120x; omitted for a
normal clip.

tools.name: export_edge_recording
tools.description:
Export a recording from a Protect camera's own (edge) storage, in two steps.

Action "prepare" sends GET /edge-recording/{camera_id}/prepare with filename, start
and end (the console requires all three; start and end are epoch SECONDS sent as
ms); the console creates an export job, copies that window off the camera and answers
        {filename, expiresAfter}, without changing configuration. Prepare is never
retried. This read is allowed in
read-only mode and executes under dry-run policy. Action "download" sends GET
/edge-recording/{camera_id}/download with the same filename. Only the arguments given
are sent (start or end with download fails before any request). Returns the upstream
body verbatim: JSON or text as sent (an upstream array under result), and a file as
{content_base64, content_type, size_bytes} with the upstream Content-Type; start or end
values that look like milliseconds or are negative add _warnings.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, action (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description:
Id of the camera whose storage holds the recording, from
list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

filename.description:
Export file name, sent as filename: the name to store it under
(prepare) and to fetch (download); for example "edge-export.mp4".

start.description:
Window start for prepare, epoch SECONDS (sent as ms); for example
1760227200.

end.description: Window end for prepare, epoch SECONDS (sent as ms); for example 1760227260.

tools.name: export_protect_case
tools.description:
Export a Protect case as a zip archive, in two steps.

With action "prepare" (which needs case_id), the console creates an export job and
builds the archive without changing configuration. This read is allowed in read-only
mode and executes under dry-run policy.
Returns: for prepare, the export job verbatim ({id, type: "CaseExport", status,
progressRatio, archiveFileName, ...}); for action "download" (needs export_id, the
job id), {content_base64, content_type, size_bytes} for the finished zip. A download before
the archive is ready, or of a large archive, can time out at the cloud connector
(HTTP 408 DeviceTimeout); try again later.

Required arguments: host, action.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

case_id.description:
Case id from list_protect_cases, for prepare only (with download it fails
before any request); for example
"000000000000000000000c01".

export_id.description:
Export job id returned by prepare, for download only (with prepare it
fails before any request); for example
"000000000000000000000d01".

tools.name: get_camera_adoption_qr
tools.description:
Get the QR code a new Protect camera scans to join WiFi and adopt to this console.

Sends GET /cameras/qr with ssid and password (wifi_password) only when given.
Protect 7.3 and later serve no QR route and answer 404 (camera "qr" not found);
that error keeps the upstream text and adds a hint (use the UniFi Protect app).
Returns the upstream body verbatim: JSON as sent (an upstream array under result),
or an image as {content_base64, content_type, size_bytes} with the upstream
Content-Type. wifi_password is a registered credential: always scrubbed from logs,
and masked in errors only under UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS.

Required arguments: host (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

ssid.description:
WiFi network name the camera should join, sent as ssid; for example
"Cameras-IoT".

wifi_password.description:
WiFi password for that network, sent as password; for example
"correct-horse-battery".

tools.name: get_camera_analytics
tools.description:
Get a Protect camera's analytics over a time window.

Kind "detections" reads GET /cameras/{camera_id}/analytics-detections (detection
counts, bucketed by step); kind "heatmap" reads analytics-heatmap (heatmap_type
sent as type). start and end are epoch SECONDS, sent as epoch milliseconds.
Returns the upstream body verbatim, and an image as {content_base64,
content_type, size_bytes}. _warnings is added (one entry per such time
argument) only when start or end is negative or looks like epoch milliseconds;
an array body then is returned under result.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, kind, start, end (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

start.description: Window start, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760227200.

end.description: Window end, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760313600.

step.description:
Detection bucket width in MILLISECONDS (the unit start and end are sent
in), sent as given without conversion; for example 3600000 (1 hour).

heatmap_type.description: Heatmap object type, sent as type; for example "person".

tools.name: get_camera_lux
tools.description:
Get a Protect camera's current light level (lux) reading.

Sends GET /cameras/{camera_id}/lux. Returns the upstream body verbatim (an
upstream array is returned under result).

Required arguments: host, camera_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

tools.name: get_camera_playback_history
tools.description:
Get a Protect camera's recording (playback) history over a time window.

Sends GET /cameras/{camera_id}/playback-history with start and end (epoch
SECONDS, sent as epoch milliseconds) and resolution (the recording quality channel,
not a time span) only when given. Returns the upstream body verbatim. _warnings is
added (one entry per such time argument) only when start or end is negative or looks
like epoch milliseconds; an array body then is returned under result.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, start, end (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

start.description: Window start, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760227200.

end.description: Window end, epoch SECONDS; for example 1760313600.

resolution.description:
Recording quality channel whose segments to list, sent as given:
0 = high quality (HQ), 2 = low quality (LQ), the values the Protect web app
sends (its enum also has 1 = AUTO); not a time span; for example 0.

tools.name: get_camera_private

Read the complete private camera settings. The relay returns status, contentType and the

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number.

Example call (get_camera_private):
    {"host": "my-console", "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id (24-hex) from list_cameras (id), e.g.
"00000000000000000000010b", or an unambiguous camera name such as "Front Door".

tools.name: get_camera_share_link
tools.description:
Read a camera's current livestream share link and status.

Cloud-only: GET protect/api/cameras/{id}/sharedStream through the Fabric connector.
No request body. Returns the upstream body verbatim. Object bodies are returned
directly as structured output; arrays use {result: body}, and an empty body uses
{result: null}. String, integer and boolean bodies have structured_content=None
and are returned as text content.
Expiry and maxStreams are server configuration (defaults 24 hours and 1 stream),
not tool parameters. The share URL/token is a bearer secret: keep it out of logs,
evidence and fixtures. This is a read and does not enable sharing.

Example call (get_camera_share_link):
    {"host": "my-console", "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b"}

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id. Resolved to its owning Fabric API key and console id before the camera request.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id from list_cameras, e.g. "00000000000000000000010b";
pass the full id, not a camera name or Network device UUID.

tools.name: get_camera_snapshot
tools.description:
Get a snapshot from a Protect camera. Returns MCP ImageContent plus image metadata.

Returns MCP ImageContent plus text and structured metadata
{image_base64, content_type, size_bytes}; content_type is the upstream
Content-Type header (typically image/jpeg), not assumed, and null when the upstream
sends none. channel and high_quality are the spec's optional query parameters, sent only
when given. With ts the tool reads a past moment from the private Protect route
cameras/{id}/recording-snapshot instead of the live frame (see ts below for its
provenance).

Example call (get_camera_snapshot):
    {"host": "my-console", "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id. Get it from list_cameras (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a
Network device UUID.

channel.description:
Optional camera channel (query channel): 'main', or 'package' for the package
camera of a camera whose hasPackageCamera is true. Sent verbatim; omit for the
controller default.

high_quality.description:
Optional (query highQuality): true forces a 1080p-or-higher snapshot, false
does not. Omit for the controller default.

ts.description:
Optional moment to snapshot, sent as query ts to the private route
cameras/{id}/recording-snapshot instead of the live snapshot. Provenance: probed
on a live console 2026-10-17 (Protect 5.3.18), where the route answered 400 without
ts and 404 "Recording not found" with it, so the key is accepted; the unit is
inferred to be epoch milliseconds and is unverified, and a returned image has not
been observed. Omit for the live frame. Example: `1760140800000`.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

configuration, so it stays available in read-only mode. Returns: the upstream

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

tools.description:

The section selects the GET route: "search" -> protect/api/detection-search, "labels" ->
protect/api/detection-search/labels (the searchable labels), "progress" ->
protect/api/detection-search/progress (indexing progress). The upstream body is

Returns the upstream body unchanged (an object or an array).

Required arguments: host.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

section.description: Which detection-search route to read, e.g. "progress".

tools.name: get_detection_statistics
tools.description:
Read Protect detection statistics, per camera, in time buckets.

Protect 7.3 requires start, end and period; an upstream rejection adds a hint.
GET protect/api/statistics/detections. start and end are epoch SECONDS and period
is an integer bucket width in SECONDS (sent as milliseconds) or a string sent
unchanged (_warnings flags start/end values that look like milliseconds or are negative).
group_id is forwarded as given; the upstream judges it. The upstream body is
returned unchanged.
Returns the upstream body unchanged (an object or an array) plus _warnings for
suspect epoch values on an object.

Required arguments: host.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

start.description: Window start, epoch seconds, e.g. 1718000000.

end.description: Window end, epoch seconds, e.g. 1718086400.

period.description: Integer bucket width in seconds, or a string forwarded unchanged; e.g. 900.

group_id.description: Recognition group id sent as groupId, e.g. "face_90".

tools.description:
Get Protect application metadata (GET /v1/meta/info via Fabric proxy). Read-only.

Returns the upstream meta-info ({applicationVersion, ...}) object verbatim, exactly as the API

Reports the Protect application version and Integration-API capabilities — the

tools.description:

GET protect/api/automations/{automation_id}/history. limit is forwarded unchanged

unchanged (an array arrives as {result: [...]}).

Required arguments: host, automation_id.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

limit.description:
Upstream history limit query parameter. Omit for the upstream default.
Example: `50`.

tools.name: get_protect_bootstrap
tools.description:
Get the Protect bootstrap: the console's whole application state in one object.

Reads GET /bootstrap on the private Protect API (the official API has no
equivalent). Returns the object verbatim and complete, never truncated: nvr,
cameras, lights, sensors, doorlocks, chimes, viewers, bridges, speakers, aiports,
users, groups, liveviews and the other collections the console sends (a bare array
would be returned as {result, _count}). It is large
on a large deployment. Camera share links and tokens in it are registered credentials:
masked only when UNIFI_REDACT_SECRETS is on, otherwise verbatim.

Required arguments: host (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

tools.name: get_protect_case_activity
tools.description:
Get the activity (audit) log of a Protect case.

Returns {activities: [...], _count} with each entry unchanged (timestamp in epoch
ms, sequenceId, description.messageRaw, ipAddress). Every links.next page is
drained by default in batches up to 100. page_size=N returns records
[(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist, fewer only at the end,
never more. page is the 1-based window number counted in units of page_size
(default 1); without page_size, returns one native console page.
To continue, resume from _nextPage with the same page_size. _pageSize reports requested,
sent, effective and returned sizes. Incomplete drains carry incomplete/incompleteReason.

Required arguments: host, case_id.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

case_id.description: Case id from list_protect_cases; for example "000000000000000000000c01".

page.description:
1-based window number counted in units of page_size (default 1); without
page_size, returns one native console page; resume from _nextPage with the same
page_size. Example: `2`.

page_size.description:
N returns records [(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist,
fewer only at the end, never more; resume from _nextPage with the same page_size.
Example: `50`.

tools.name: get_protect_case_asset_snapshot
tools.description:
Get the snapshot image of a Protect case asset.

Returns {image_base64, content_type, size_bytes}. Not served by every Protect
version: on Protect 7.x through the cloud connector the route answers HTTP 404
(route not found), which is returned as the upstream error.

Required arguments: host, case_id, asset_id.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

tools.name: get_protect_stream_url

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

livestream, playback, timelapse, heatmap, live_detect_track, live_alias or

channel.description:
Camera channel index (0 is the highest quality; livestream defaults

end.description: Window end, epoch SECONDS (sent as ms); for example 1760227260.

lens.description: Lens index of a multi-lens camera; for example 0.

stream_type.description:
Sent as type, for example "fmp4" (livestream) or "rotating"
(video_prepare); for example "fmp4".
