tools.name: list_protect_events
tools.description:
Query historical Protect events via private /proxy/protect/api/events; the official
Integration events endpoint is WebSocket-only.

Returns drained object pages preserving data and the first page's envelope fields, adding _count
and _warnings. A drain of bare arrays returns {result, _count} with _warnings when applicable.
Capped drains also carry incomplete/incompleteReason. An explicit offset/limit fetches one page
when offset is supplied: a bare list stays a list (without warnings); an object page
preserves every upstream top-level field verbatim, including data and totalCount, adding
only _count and _warnings. Sensor events retain sensor:null and gain _resolved_sensor from
metadata.sensorId.text. All event fields and identifiers are preserved.
Object pages carry epoch-unit and smart-detect _warnings, as drained results do.

Required host/start/end; time is integer epoch SECONDS, never ISO strings or
milliseconds. Negative or millisecond-magnitude times are not refused: they are
converted to milliseconds like any time and object results carry _warnings.
query_isp_metrics instead takes ISO 8601 strings. Face names are at
metadata.detectedThumbnails[].matchedName. types, smart_detect_types and categories are
forwarded as given (empty list sends no parameter); empty cameras applies no filter. Full
examples: docs/TOOL-USAGE.md#list_protect_events.

Required arguments: host, start, end (see parameter descriptions for identifiers).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

start.description:
REQUIRED. Epoch SECONDS (UTC) as integers, converted to milliseconds internally.
Bounds are exact millisecond instants; end excludes the remainder of its second.
History depth is bounded by the NVR's retention.
(Contrast query_isp_metrics, which wants ISO 8601 strings.)

end.description:
REQUIRED. Epoch SECONDS (UTC) as integers, converted to milliseconds internally. Ranges
are exact millisecond instants; end excludes the remainder of its second.
History depth is bounded by the NVR's retention. (Contrast
query_isp_metrics, which wants ISO 8601 strings.)

types.description:
Filter by event TYPE; single value or a list. Verified-present values: motion,
smartDetectZone, smartAudioDetect, sensorOpened, sensorClosed, access. Smart-detect
subtypes (person, face, animal, alrmSpeak and so on) are not event types; pass them in
smart_detect_types instead. An unrecognised value returns zero events.
Shape: string|string[]

cameras.description:
filter by camera NAME or ID; single value or list. Names resolve to IDs: an exact
match first, then Unicode-normalized (NFC) and case-insensitive, then ignoring
surrounding whitespace (case kept before case-insensitive); an unknown name errors
(listing the camera names as the console has them) rather than silently matching
nothing.
Shape: string|string[]

limit.description:
Without offset, the event count gathered from the beginning across pages;
fewer only when the window ends. With offset, limit is sent unchanged as one
page. No size clamp is measured on this feed. _pageSize reports the requested
count, the size sent on each request, the observed effective size and the
returned count. Omit limit and offset to drain all events; the only page cap is
opt-in UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES, which marks an early stop incomplete.
Example: `25`.

offset.description:
Zero-based starting record. Fetches one page: with limit, limit is sent
unchanged as that page size (not collected across pages). Omit both to drain every
event for the window. The opt-in UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES marks an early stop
incomplete; no default page cap applies.
Example: `25`.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort order sent as orderDirection: "ASC" (oldest-first) or "DESC"
(newest-first). Omitted (default): no orderDirection is sent and the upstream's own
order applies.

smart_detect_types.description:
filter by the smart-detect SUBTYPE — person, vehicle, animal, package,
face, licensePlate (on smartDetectZone events) and the audio alarms alrmSpeak,
alrmSiren, alrmBark, alrmCarHorn (on smartAudioDetect events). This is a distinct
upstream parameter from types. The API only honours it when types is also set to the
relevant event type(s); passing smart_detect_types alone is a silent no-op upstream:
it is still sent, and the result carries a _warnings entry
(SMART_DETECT_TYPES_WITHOUT_TYPES). Example: types="smartDetectZone",
smart_detect_types="person" for just person detections; types="smartAudioDetect",
smart_detect_types="alrmSpeak" to isolate the dominant audio-alarm noise.
Shape: string|string[]

categories.description:
filter by event category; single value or list. Verified values: motion, smart,
iot, admin. Unknown values are silently ignored by the upstream API.
Shape: string|string[]

without_descriptions.description:
when true, ask the API to omit each event's description block (~16%
smaller payload). Opt-in only — full-fidelity records are the default and descriptions
are never dropped automatically.

tools.name: list_recognition_detections
tools.description:
List one enrolled recognition group's detections (sightings) on Protect.

Returns {detections, _count} plus upstream envelope fields and epoch warnings.
Required group_id comes from list_recognition_groups, for example face_90. There
is no all-groups mode; a nonexistent group returns HTTP 404. Each detection has
id, eventId (list_protect_events), thumbnailId (get_thumbnail), detectedAt (epoch
milliseconds), cameraId and matchedGroupConfidence (0-100).

Default drains all links.next pages in batches up to 100. page_size=N returns
records [(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist, fewer only at the
end, never more. page is the 1-based window number counted in units of page_size
(default 1); without page_size, returns one native console page.
To continue, resume from _nextPage with the same page_size. _pageSize reports requested,
sent, effective and returned sizes. Incomplete drains carry incomplete/incompleteReason.

The page without page_size fetches one native page, with _nextPage when more exist.
An explicit page keeps a bare list verbatim (no _warnings) when page_size is absent,
and preserves every field of an object page verbatim with epoch-unit _warnings.
A bare-list manual page is unchanged without _warnings; object pages preserve
upstream fields and add epoch warnings.
Examples are in docs/TOOL-USAGE.md#list_recognition_detections.

Required arguments: host, type, group_id.

host.description:
Console reportedState.hostname or data[].id from list_hosts, for example "my-console";
names match reportedState.hostname/name case-insensitively.

type.description: 'face' or 'vehicle' (singular); plural forms return HTTP 400 upstream.

group_id.description: Group id from list_recognition_groups, for example 'face_90'.

page_size.description:
N returns records [(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist,
fewer only at the end, never more; resume from _nextPage with the same page_size.
Example: `100`.

start.description:
Optional UTC epoch seconds start, converted to milliseconds. Negative
or millisecond-magnitude values add _warnings. Example: 1792972800.

end.description:
Optional UTC epoch seconds end, converted to milliseconds; omit both for
all detections. The same magnitude warnings apply. Example: 1793059200.

page.description:
1-based window number counted in units of page_size (default 1); without
page_size, returns one native console page; resume from _nextPage with the same
page_size. Example: `2`.

tools.name: list_recognition_groups

Returns {groups, _count} plus upstream envelope fields. Each group has a stable
monotonic id (for example face_90), name/matchedName, detectionsCount, and
createdAt/firstDetectedAt/lastDetectedAt timestamps. Names remain unchanged.
The private recognition API returns groups under groups, rather than data.

Default drains all links.next pages in batches up to 100. page_size=N returns
records [(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist, fewer only at the
end, never more. page is the 1-based window number counted in units of page_size
(default 1); without page_size, returns one native console page.
To continue, resume from _nextPage with the same page_size. _pageSize reports requested,
sent, effective and returned sizes. Incomplete drains carry incomplete/incompleteReason.

Required arguments: host, type.

host.description:
Console reportedState.hostname or data[].id from list_hosts, for example "my-console";
names match reportedState.hostname/name case-insensitively.

type.description:
Recognition type, normally 'face' or 'vehicle' (singular). Forwarded
unchanged; plural forms return HTTP 400 from upstream.

has_name.description: When true, return named groups only. Example: true.

page_size.description:
N returns records [(page-1)*N, page*N): exactly N when that many exist,
fewer only at the end, never more; resume from _nextPage with the same page_size.
Example: `100`.

order_by.description:
Sort field: name, createdAt, lastDetectedAt or detectionsCount.
Example: 'name'. With no order_direction, upstream defaults to descending.

order_direction.description:
'asc' or 'desc', case-insensitive; effective only with
order_by. Unknown values return upstream HTTP 400. Example: 'asc'.

page.description:
1-based window number counted in units of page_size (default 1); without
page_size, returns one native console page; resume from _nextPage with the same
page_size. Example: `2`.

tools.name: merge_recognition_groups
tools.description:
Merge Protect recognition groups into one.

POST protect/api/recognition/{type}/merge-group with the body the Protect web app
sends, {"fromGroupIds": from_group_ids, "toGroupId": to_group_id}; the upstream
response is returned unchanged. An empty or non-list from_group_ids, an empty
to_group_id, or a from_group_ids list that names to_group_id is refused before any
request. Under dry-run policy it returns a dry-run preview.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny.
Consequence: the groups in from_group_ids are folded into to_group_id with their
detections; there is no unmerge.
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null); under
dry-run policy the preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params, body}}.

Required arguments: host, type.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

type.description: Recognition type, singular; plural forms return HTTP 400 upstream, e.g. "face".

to_group_id.description:
Id of the group that is kept, from list_recognition_groups,
e.g. "face_90".

from_group_ids.description: Shape: string[]. Ids of the groups merged into it, e.g. ["face_91"].

merge.description:
Legacy native body sent verbatim when supplied instead of the typed
arguments; it takes precedence, so to_group_id and from_group_ids are then ignored.
Free-form object. Shape: {fromGroupIds:string[],toGroupId:string}.

tools.name: move_ptz_camera
tools.description:

Sends movement as given to POST cameras/{camera_id}/move on the Protect console
host. The web app builds this body at run time and no published schema documents
it, so no key is required or added; the console validates it and its error is
returned in full. To go to a saved position use ptz_goto_preset; to return home use
ptz_home. Returns {status: "sent", response}. Sent once, never auto-retried on 429.
With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)} and sends no
write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Consequence: the camera physically moves, so its view and any running patrol or
auto-tracking change at once.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: PTZ camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

movement.description:
Movement object sent as given (free-form; shape not published); for
example {"type": "continuous", "payload": {"x": 10, "y": 0, "z": 0}}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: play_chime_sound

Consequence: the chime sounds aloud in the building.

Output "speaker" sends POST /chimes/{chime_id}/play-speaker with options as the
body (the web UI builds it at run time, so it is free-form and sent as given, for
example ringtone and volume); output "buzzer" sends POST /chimes/{chime_id}/
play-buzzer. Private Protect API (no official route). Sent once. Returns {status:
"played", response} with the upstream body verbatim. With dry-run policy, returns
{status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include body
and params.

Required arguments: host, chime_id, output (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

chime_id.description:
Chime id (24-hex) from list_chimes; for example
"000000000000000000000110".

options.description:
Speaker body sent as given (free-form object); for example
{"volume": 60}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: pos_ingest_transaction
tools.description:
Ingest a POS transaction overlay onto camera footage.

Consequence: the transaction is overlaid on the camera's recorded footage.

Returns {status: "sent", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON,
the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

Route: POST /v1/pos/cameras/{id}/transactions (Fabric proxy).

WARNING: creates a footage overlay event with no documented rollback. The transaction is
validated locally and carries an idempotency key; the POS write is never auto-retried.
`transaction`: REQUIRED posTransactionRequest object. Must include `type`
  ('sale'|'refund'), `externalId` (per-camera unique idempotency/dedup key), and
  `amount`; optional currency/lineItems/location/paymentTypes/timestamp pass through.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/pos/cameras/{id}/transactions; schema
"posTransactionRequest") is passed in `transaction`. Required keys — type, externalId, amount.
- type: enum[sale|refund]
- externalId: string
- amount: number
- currency: string (uppercase ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD)
- lineItems: array of object, at most 200 items {title: string (1-255 characters),
  quantity: integer (>= 1)} (both item keys required)
- location: object {id: string (1-255 characters, required), name: string (1-255
  characters)}
- paymentTypes: array of string
- timestamp: integer (epoch ms; within the last 24 hours and at most 5 minutes ahead of
  server time, else rejected)

Example call (pos_ingest_transaction):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "camera_id": "00000000000000000000010b",
      "transaction": {"type": "sale", "externalId": "order-1042", "amount": 24.95}
    }

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

camera_id.description:
Protect camera id. Get it from list_cameras (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a
Network device UUID.

transaction.description:
posTransactionRequest (Protect 7.3.74). Required: type ('sale'|'refund'),
externalId (per-camera unique dedup key), amount. Never auto-retried.
Advisory spec fields; any JSON passes. A POS transaction to overlay on camera footage Required: amount, externalId, type.

currency.description: Uppercase ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD

externalId.description: Caller-supplied transaction id, unique per camera.

timestamp.description: Transaction time in epoch milliseconds; within the past 24 hours and no more than 5 minutes in the future.

type.description: Transaction type One of: 'sale', 'refund'.

confirm.description: Ignored. The call runs when made; there is no confirmation step.

device_type.description:
Protect device type: aiport, aiprocessor, camera, chime, doorlock,
light, linkstation, sensor, speaker or viewer; for example "camera".

device_id.description:
Protect device id (24-hex) from the device's list tool or
get_protect_bootstrap; for example "00000000000000000000010b".

reset.description: Also reset the device to defaults, sent as ?reset=; for example false.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: reboot_nvr
tools.description:
Reboot the Protect NVR once. All camera recording and live view are interrupted until it
returns. Returns the relay status and complete upstream body. No automatic retry; a
timeout means outcome unknown, read back before retrying.

Consequence: the NVR restarts, so no camera footage is recorded and live view is unavailable
until it is back; that gap in footage cannot be recovered. No setting is changed.

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.
Write metadata includes writeEnabled; _warnings describes operational risks.

Under dry-run policy no upstream write is sent: status is "dry_run" and body
contains the exact preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params (query parameters), body}}.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number or dry_run for a preview.

Example call (reboot_nvr):
    {"host": "my-console"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

tools.name: reboot_protect_device
tools.description:
Reboot a Protect device once. Camera recording and live view are interrupted while it
restarts. No automatic retry; a timeout means outcome unknown, read back before
retrying.

Consequence: the camera or sensor restarts and is offline until it comes back; a camera
records nothing and serves no live view meanwhile, and that gap in footage cannot be
recovered. No setting is changed.

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.
Write metadata includes writeEnabled; _warnings describes operational risks.

Under dry-run policy no upstream write is sent: status is "dry_run" and body
contains the exact preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params (query parameters), body}}.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number or dry_run for a preview.

Example call (reboot_protect_device):
    {"host": "my-console", "device_type": "camera", "device_id": "00000000000000000000010b"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

device_type.description:
Protect resource kind, singular: "camera" or "sensor" (the route
adds the plural collection, e.g. protect/api/cameras).

device_id.description:
Protect device id (24-hex) from list_cameras / list_sensors (id),
e.g. "00000000000000000000010b", or an unambiguous device name such as
"Front Door".

tools.name: recognize_image
tools.description:
Run Protect recognition on an uploaded image.

Sends the decoded image as a multipart file part with POST
protect/api/recognition/recognize-image; the upstream response (what Protect
recognised) is returned unchanged. This is a POST, so it is classed as a write.
Invalid base64 is refused before any request. Under dry-run policy it returns a
dry-run preview (part name, filename, type and size).
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny.
Consequence: the image is uploaded to and processed by the console.
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null), a binary
answer as {image_base64, content_type, size_bytes}; under dry-run policy the
preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params,
body}}.

Required arguments: host, filename, file_content_base64.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

filename.description: File name sent with the part, e.g. "photo.jpg".

content_type.description:
Part MIME type, e.g. "image/jpeg". Omit to derive it from the
filename extension.

form_field.description:
Multipart field name, default "file" (the published Protect
upload's name), e.g. "file".

tools.name: reformat_edge_storage
tools.description:
Reformat a Protect camera's own (edge) recording storage.

Sends POST /edge-recording/{camera_id}/reformat, once (never retried). Returns
{status: "sent", response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: irreversible: erases every recording on the camera's own storage.

Required arguments: host, camera_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description:
Id of the camera whose storage to reformat, from list_cameras;
for example "000000000000000000000103".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: relay_activate_output
tools.description:
Switch a relay output (POST /v1/relays/{id}/outputs/{outputId}/activate).

Consequence: whatever is wired to the relay output (door lock, gate, light) acts in the real
world.

Returns {status: "sent", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON,
the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

WARNING: physically switches hardware.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, POST /v1/relays/{id}/outputs/{outputId}/activate; schema "inline
requestBody schema") is built from scalar parameters. No key is required; send only the keys to
change.
- state: enum[on|off]
- pulseDuration: integer (ms)

Example call (relay_activate_output):
    {"host": "my-console", "relay_id": "00000000000000000000010b", "output_id": 0}

The dry-run preview contains method, path, params (query parameters), and body.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

relay_id.description:
Protect relay id. Get it from list_relays (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a
Network device UUID.

output_id.description:
Output channel id on that device; spec: integer 0 or 1 (an integer, or the same
value as a decimal string '0'|'1'). See get_relay.

confirm.description: Ignored. The call runs when made; there is no confirmation step.

state.description: 'on' or 'off'; omit to toggle (spec body state).

pulse_duration.description:
Auto-off after N ms (spec body pulseDuration, >=0). The spec applies it
only when state is 'on'; the server sends it as given and does not check state.

tools.name: remove_protect_case_asset
tools.description:
Remove one asset from a Protect case (the recording stays on the NVR).

Consequence: the asset leaves the case for every user; add it again with
add_protect_case_asset. The recording itself stays on the NVR.

Sends DELETE /cases/{case_id}/assets/{asset_id}. Returns {deleted: true, message,
response}. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", deleted: false,
message, response: PREVIEW} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, case_id, asset_id.

Returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is true, message summarizes the delete, and response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON, raw text, or null when the body is empty).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

case_id.description: Case id from list_protect_cases; for example "000000000000000000000c01".

asset_id.description:
Asset id from list_protect_case_assets; for example
"000000000000000000000a01".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: report_ai_false_positive
tools.description:
Report a Protect AI detection as a false positive.

POST protect/api/report/ai-false-positive with {"eventId": event_id,
"reportedThumbnails": reported_thumbnails} (the keys the frontend sends); the
upstream response is returned unchanged. Under dry-run policy it returns a dry-run
preview. Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny.
Consequence: the report and the named thumbnails are submitted from the console.
Returns the upstream response unchanged (an object, an array or null); under
dry-run policy the preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params, body}}.

Required arguments: host, event_id, reported_thumbnails.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

reported_thumbnails.description:
Non-empty list of thumbnails of the event being reported, sent
as given (an empty list fails before any request), for example
["e-000000000000000000000117"].
Shape: (string|object)[]; keys the server reads: none, each entry is sent as given

tools.name: reset_camera_image_settings
tools.description:
Reset a Protect camera's image (ISP) settings to their defaults.

Sends POST /cameras/{camera_id}/reset-isp, once. Returns {status: "reset",
response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: discards the camera's tuned image settings; they are not restored.

Required arguments: host, camera_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: reset_protect_automations
tools.description:
Reset the console's Protect automations to the upstream defaults.

POST protect/api/automations/reset with no body. Returns: the upstream response
unchanged.

Consequence: the current configuration is replaced by the upstream defaults, and
custom entries are lost unless recreated.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: restore_protect_backup
tools.description:
Restore a stored Protect backup, replacing the live Protect configuration.

POST protect/api/backup/{backup_id}/restore with no body (the singular route;
Protect 7.3 answers 404 on the plural one). The upstream judges backup_id.
Returns: the upstream response unchanged.

Consequence: the live Protect configuration is replaced by the backup's;
irreversible, and Protect may restart, interrupting recording while it does.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host, backup_id.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: restore_protect_database
tools.description:
Restore the Protect database from its stored database dump.

POST protect/api/nvr/restore-pg-dump with no body. Returns: the upstream response
unchanged.

Consequence: the live Protect database is replaced by the stored dump, losing
changes made since it; irreversible, and Protect may restart.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: search_detections
tools.description:
Search Protect detections with a natural-language description.

GET protect/api/detection-nls with searchText and only the filters given. start and
end are epoch SECONDS, sent as milliseconds (_warnings flags values that look like
milliseconds or are negative). cameras takes camera ids or names (names resolve to
ids; an unknown name fails listing the cameras). Without limit/offset every page is
drained (incomplete=true with the reason if a drain stops short); with either, that
one page is returned in the upstream shape.
Returns a drained list as {data or result, _count} plus the first page's other
fields, incomplete and incompleteReason when it stopped short, and _warnings; an
explicit page as the upstream page plus _count and _warnings (a bare-array page
as that array).

A searchHost 404 indicates detection search service availability or configuration;
check Protect.

Required arguments: host, search_text.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

search_text.description: What to look for, e.g. "white van in the driveway".

start.description: Window start, epoch seconds, e.g. 1718000000.

end.description: Window end, epoch seconds, e.g. 1718003600.

cameras.description:
Camera ids or names, e.g. ["000000000000000000000114"].
Shape: string[]

min_similarity.description: minSimilarity threshold sent as given, e.g. 0.25.

order_by.description: orderBy value sent as given, e.g. "similarity".

limit.description: Page size for one explicit page. Example: `50`.

offset.description: Start position for one explicit page. Example: `25`.

tools.name: search_recognition_group_candidates
tools.description:
Search for recognition groups that are candidates for a match or merge.

GET protect/api/recognition/{type}/groups/search-candidates. The inventory records
no fixed query keys, so query_params is a free-form object forwarded as query parameters
exactly as given (omit it to send none). The upstream body is returned unchanged.
Returns the upstream body unchanged (an object or an array).

Required arguments: host, type.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

type.description: Use "face" or "vehicle" (singular; plural forms return HTTP 400 upstream).

query_params.description: Free-form query parameters, e.g. {"groupId": "face_90"}. Omit for none.

tools.name: set_ai_port_pairing
tools.description:
Pair cameras with an AI Port (paired=true) or unpair them (paired=false).

Consequence: paired cameras get the AI Port's smart detections; unpaired cameras
lose them until paired again.

Sends {cameraIds} to POST /aiports/{aiport_id}/pair or /unpair on the private
Protect API (no official route). Sent once. Returns {status: "paired" or
"unpaired", response} with the upstream body verbatim. With dry-run policy, returns
{status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW} and sends no write. Dry-run response
previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, aiport_id, camera_ids, paired (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

aiport_id.description:
AI Port id (24-hex) from get_protect_bootstrap aiports; for example
"00000000000000000000010c".

camera_ids.description:
Non-empty list of camera ids sent as cameraIds (an empty list fails
before any request); for example ["00000000000000000000010b"].

paired.description: true pairs, false unpairs; for example true.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_camera_control_enabled
tools.description:
Enable or disable control of a Protect camera.

Sends GET /cameras/{camera_id}/enable-control (enabled=true) or disable-control
(false). The console changes state on this GET, so it is a write: refused under
read-only mode and the Protect write opt-out, and sent once (never retried).
Returns {status: "enabled" | "disabled", response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: changes whether the camera can be controlled until it is set back.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, enabled (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

enabled.description:
true sends enable-control, false sends disable-control; for example
false.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_camera_door_lock
tools.description:
Lock or unlock the door lock connected to a Protect camera (a doorbell or access
reader with a lock).

Sends POST /cameras/{camera_id}/lock (locked=true) or /unlock (false), once.
Returns {status: "locked" | "unlocked", response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: physically locks or unlocks the door; unlocking lets anyone in.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, locked (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

locked.description: true locks, false unlocks; for example true.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_camera_resolution_scale
tools.description:
Set a Protect camera's resolution scale.

Sends POST /cameras/{camera_id}/resolutionScale/{scale}, once; the console judges
the value. Returns {status: "sent", response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: changes the resolution the camera streams and records at.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, scale (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

scale.description: Scale value sent as one path segment; for example "1".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_camera_video_codec
tools.description:
Set the video codec a Protect camera encodes with.

Sends POST /cameras/{camera_id}/videoCodec?name=CODEC, once; the console judges
the codec name. Returns {status: "sent", response} (response is the upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: changes the codec of the camera's streams and new recordings.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, codec (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

codec.description: Codec name, sent as the name query parameter; for example "h265".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_door_lock_auto_close
tools.description:
Set or trigger a UniFi door lock's auto-close (auto-relock) behaviour.

Consequence: changes when the door locks itself again, which affects physical
access to the door.

Sends POST /doorlocks/{doorlock_id}/autoClose on the private Protect API (no
official route). The web UI builds the body at run time, so options is sent as
given (free-form object) and nothing is sent when omitted. Sent once. Returns
{status: "sent", response} with the upstream body verbatim. With dry-run policy,
returns {status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include
body and params.

Required arguments: host, doorlock_id (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

doorlock_id.description:
Door lock id (24-hex) from list_door_locks; for example
"000000000000000000000111".

options.description:
Request body sent as given (free-form object); for example
{"autoCloseTimeMs": 15000}.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_door_lock_state
tools.description:
Unlock (action="open") or lock (action="close") a UniFi door lock.

Consequence: open physically unlocks the door, so anyone can enter until it is
locked again or auto-close relocks it; close locks it.

Sends POST /doorlocks/{doorlock_id}/open or /close on the private Protect API (no
official route); no body. Sent once, never auto-retried. Returns {status: "opened"
or "closed", response} with the upstream body verbatim; read lockStatus back with
list_door_locks. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response:
PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, doorlock_id, action (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

doorlock_id.description:
Door lock id (24-hex) from list_door_locks; for example
"000000000000000000000111".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_edge_storage_mount_state
tools.description:
Mount or unmount a Protect camera's own (edge) recording storage.

Sends POST /edge-recording/{camera_id}/mount-state with {mountState}, once; the
console judges the value. Returns {status: "sent", response} (response is the
upstream body verbatim).
With dry-run policy, returns a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun, sent: false,
message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} and sends nothing.

Consequence: an unmounted card stops on-camera recording until it is mounted.

Required arguments: host, camera_id, mount_state (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description:
Id of the camera whose storage to mount or unmount, from
list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

mount_state.description:
Value sent as mountState: "unmounted" unmounts the storage and "mounted"
mounts it again (the console judges the value); for example "unmounted".

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_nvr_stack_membership
tools.description:
Add a console to this Protect NVR stack (member=true) or remove it (false).

Consequence: adding links the console's storage and cameras into this stack;
removing detaches it, and with reset=true it is also reset to defaults, erasing
its configuration.

With member=true it sends {mac} to POST /nvr-stacks/adopt; member=false sends {mac,
reset?} to POST /nvr-stacks/unadopt (private Protect API, no official route).
reset is sent only when given. Sent once, never auto-retried. Returns {status:
"adopt_requested" or "unadopt_requested", response} with the upstream body
verbatim. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW}.
Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, mac, member (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

mac.description:
MAC address of the console to add or remove, sent as mac; for example
"00:00:5e:00:53:01".

member.description: true adds the console to the stack, false removes it; for example true.

reset.description: Removal only: also reset the console to defaults; for example false.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_protect_event_favorite
tools.description:
Mark Protect events as favorite (favorite=true) or remove the mark (false).

Consequence: only the events' favorite mark changes, as every user of the console
sees it; no recording changes.

One id (a string) uses the per-event route and returns {status, response,
verified, event}: the event is read back and verified is whether isFavorite (or,
with object_id, favoriteObjectIds) now matches. A list of ids uses the batch route.
Returns {status, response}, where response maps each id to the console's result.
Both forms answer status: "favorited" for favorite=true and status: "unfavorited"
for false. The Protect write opt-out and read-only mode apply before any request.
With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", response: PREVIEW} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, event_ids, favorite.

FavoriteObject.description: One per-object favorite mark for the batch route (``idsWithObject``).

eventId.description: Id of the event to mark; one of event_ids.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

event_ids.description:
One event id, or a non-empty list of ids for the batch route (an empty
list fails before any request); for example
"000000000000000000000e01".
Shape: string|string[]

favorite.description: true to favorite, false to unfavorite; for example true.

object_id.description:
Single-id form only (with a list it fails before any request): favorite
one detected object of the event
(metadata.detectedThumbnails[].objectId); for example
"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000e02".

objects.description:
List form only (with one event id it fails before any request): per-object
marks sent as idsWithObject, each
{eventId, objectId}; for example [{"eventId": "0000...", "objectId": "0000..."}].
Shape: {eventId:string,objectId:string}[]

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

tools.name: set_protect_notification_receivers
tools.description:
Set who receives Protect system notifications.

PATCH protect/api/automations/system-notifications/receivers with receivers sent
verbatim. Returns: the upstream response unchanged. An empty object is refused
before any request.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host, receivers.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

receivers.description:
Native receivers object, e.g.
{"userIds": ["000000000000000000000113"]}. Free-form object.

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: set_protect_notifications_muted
tools.description:
Mute or unmute user notifications.

Consequence: muted, the user gets no Protect notifications until valid_until (or the
upstream default) passes or they are unmuted; unmuted, notifications resume at once.

The user_id is resolved in the Protect bootstrap users; muted true sends POST
protect/api/users/{id}/notifications/mute {validUntil}, false sends DELETE on it.
Returns: the upstream response with _before, _after, _verified, _readAfterError and

tools.name: update_camera_private
tools.description:
Change camera recording, zones, image, IR, lux index, audio, motion detection and
tracking. Read-merge-PATCH preserves nested siblings; zone arrays replace in full,
so retain every wanted zone. Privacy masks hide covered imagery.

Consequence: the PATCH persistently changes stored camera settings. Restore prior
readBefore values to reverse settings changes. Disabling recording leaves footage gaps.
Disabling motion detection loses footage only in motion- or detection-triggered recording
modes; recordingSettings.mode="always" continues recording. Privacy masks hide covered
imagery. Missing footage and masked imagery cannot be recovered later.

Returns relay method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes. Write metadata includes
writeEnabled. Read twins add readBefore/readAfter, noOp and changed when known.
_verified says requested fields saved; noOp, changed and _noOp compare requested leaves,
type-strict. If requested fields are absent from both 2xx reads, noOpReason explains why
noOp is unknown. Failed read-back leaves _verified and _noOp null; readAfterError and
_verificationWarning explain failed or unproven verification.

Under dry-run policy no write is sent. Status is "dry_run"; body contains the exact
merged preview {status, dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params,
body}}. _verified remains null; otherwise status is the upstream HTTP number.

Example call (update_camera_private):
    {"host":"my-console","camera_id":"00000000000000000000010b",
     "settings":{"recordingSettings":{"mode":"always"}}}

tools.name: update_camera_shortcut
tools.description:
Update a camera's shortcuts (PATCH cameras/{camera_id}/shortcuts).

The route has no shortcut id in its path. The camera is read first (GET
cameras/{camera_id} on the Protect console host); when body carries an id that the
camera's shortcuts array lists, a no-op returns
{status: "noop", resource}, and the read-back verifies every requested leaf
(type-strict). An id the array does not list fails listing the valid ids. Without a
locatable id the body is sent and verified is null with readAfterError. The body is
sent as a single-item array. validate_schema=true checks id, any placement x/y, and any
complete nested shortcut using the same per-type rules as create_camera_shortcut.
Returns {status: "updated", verified, before, after, response}. An empty body fails
before any request. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", before,
response (the preview)}.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Consequence: a successful request can change the shortcut buttons shown for this camera.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

camera_id.description: Camera id from list_cameras; for example "000000000000000000000103".

body.description:
One shortcut update, sent inside an array (free-form): the shortcut's id plus
the parts to change; for example {"id": "000000000000000000000109",
"placement": {"x": 0, "y": 0}}. Protect 7.3.74 rejected anything but an
array of {id, placement?, shortcut?} with an AJV 400.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

validate_schema.description: Opt in to local per-type shape checks; for example true.

tools.name: update_chime
tools.description:
Update a Protect chime: name, paired cameraIds or per-camera ringSettings (volume, ringtone).

Returns {status: "updated", verified, before, after, response}, or {status: "noop", reason,
resource} when every sent leaf already matches (no PATCH is sent). Read-before, no-op,
PATCH, read-after: before/after are the object read before and after the write, verified
is true when the read-after carries every sent leaf value (nested objects are compared
leaf by leaf, so a partial nested update verifies by the leaves
it sends; sibling keys it does not send are ignored), and response is the PATCH body
verbatim (decoded JSON, the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
verified is null, with readAfterError, when the read-after fails or cannot be matched.
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", before (the body read first), response
(the preview)}; there is no read-after.

Request body (Protect 7.3.74, PATCH /v1/chimes/{id}; schema "inline requestBody schema") is
passed in `settings`. No key is required; send only the keys to change.
- name: string
- cameraIds: array of string
- ringSettings: array of object {cameraId: string, repeatTimes: number (1-10),
  ringtoneId: string, volume: number (0-100)} (every item key required)

    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "chime_id": "00000000000000000000010b",
      "settings": {"name": "Hallway chime"}

Protect chime id. Get it from list_chimes (id). Protect id (24-hex) — not a

Partial update (PATCH; only listed keys change); spec Protect 7.3.74 PATCH
/v1/chimes/{id} body. Keys: name, cameraIds, ringSettings.
Advisory spec fields; any JSON passes.

tools.name: update_nvr
tools.description:
Change NVR doorbell custom messages, insights, analytics and retention. Nested objects
merge; arrays replace in full. DANGER: shorter recording retention can permanently
delete older footage; retention coupling is controller-dependent and needs live testing.
Returns the relay response with readBefore/readAfter, _verified and _noOp. A failed or
non-object read-after leaves _verified and _noOp null, preserving the relay error.
Dry-run previews the exact merged body.

Consequence: the PATCH persistently changes NVR-wide settings, reversible by writing back
the prior values returned in readBefore; shortening recording retention, however, can make
the NVR permanently delete older footage, which no later write restores.

Returns method, routeClass, scope, path, resolvedPath, status, contentType and
body; binary responses use bodyBase64 and sizeBytes.
Write metadata includes writeEnabled; retention changes may add _warnings.
Read twins add readBefore, readAfter, noOp and changed when known; _noOp compares
requested leaves, type-strict. If requested fields are absent from both 2xx reads,
noOpReason explains why noOp is unknown. readAfterError and _verificationWarning
explain failed or unproven read-back.

Under dry-run policy no upstream write is sent: status is "dry_run" and body
contains the exact preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview:
{method, path, params (query parameters), body}}.

Result status is the upstream HTTP number or dry_run for a preview.

Example call (update_nvr):
    {"host": "my-console", "settings": {"isInsightsEnabled": true}}

customMessages.description: Complete custom-message list; retain entries to keep them. Controller normally accepts at most 30 characters per message. Shape: string[]

autoRetentionEnabled.description: Automatic recording retention; coupled behaviour is controller-dependent.

recordingRetentionDurationMs.description: Retention duration in milliseconds as an integer or string, or null. Shortening it can permanently delete footage.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

settings.description:
Typed partial private settings, e.g.
{"isInsightsEnabled":true,"analyticsData":"anonymous"}; additional controller fields
pass through.

tools.name: update_protect_automation
tools.description:
Change fields of one Protect automation (read, merge, write, then verify).

Lists automations to find automation_id (an unknown id fails listing the valid
ids, before any write), deep-merges changes into the listed record and sends it with
PATCH protect/api/automations/{automation_id}. Returns: the upstream response
unchanged plus _before, _after and _verified (every requested leaf re-read, type
strict), and _readAfterError when the re-read failed; a non-object response is
returned whole under response with those keys beside it. An empty changes object is
refused before any request.
Honours UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:protect=deny, and returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}} (nothing sent) when dry-run policy is set.

Required arguments: host, automation_id, changes.

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

changes.description:
Fields to change, nested as on the record, e.g. {"enabled": false}.
Free-form object.

confirm.description:
Accepted and ignored; kept for compatibility. It never gates the
call, e.g. true.

tools.name: update_protect_case
tools.description:
Update a Protect case: rename, edit the summary, close (active=false) or reopen.

Requested top-level fields are sent (PATCH /cases/{case_id}), preserving current
nested siblings; a fields key that a typed argument also sets fails before any
request. Read-back verifies all merged leaves type-strictly. The case is read from
list_protect_cases before and after. Returns {status: "updated", verified, before,
after, response}, or {status: "noop", resource} when every field already matches.
Passing no field fails before any request. With dry-run policy, returns {status:
"dry_run", before, response: PREVIEW} and sends no write.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, case_id.

host.description: Protect console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (for example "Home NVR") or data[].id.

case_id.description: Case id from list_protect_cases; for example "000000000000000000000c01".

name.description: New case name; for example "Garage break-in (closed)".

active.description: false closes the case, true reopens it; for example false.

fields.description:
Other case fields sent as given (free-form object); for example
{"incidentSeverity": "high"}.
A key a typed argument also sets fails before any request.

confirm.description: Accepted and ignored for compatibility; for example false.

Update a Protect case asset: note, title or whether it is included in exports.

Sends PATCH /cases/{case_id}/assets/{asset_id}, preserving current nested siblings.
Read-back verifies all merged leaves type-strictly. The
console requires the asset type in every PATCH, so the asset's current type is sent
when asset_type is omitted (as the Protect web app does). The asset is read from
list_protect_case_assets before and after. Returns {status: "updated", verified,
before, after, response} or {status: "noop", resource}. No field fails before any
request. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", before, response: PREVIEW}.

Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, case_id, asset_id.

case_id.description: Case id from list_protect_cases; for example "000000000000000000000c01".

Asset id from list_protect_case_assets; for example
"000000000000000000000a01".

Include the asset in case exports, sent as includeInExport;
for example false.

Type discriminator to send (clip, externalFile, pdfReport,
presentation); for example "clip".

{"isMuted": true}.

tools.description:
Set the NVR device password. Consequence: integrations can require updating.

tools.name: update_protect_device_settings
tools.description:
Update settings of any Protect device type with read-back verification.

Types bridge, camera, chime, light, linkstation, sensor, speaker and viewer use the
official PATCH /v1/{family}/{id} (spec Protect 7.3.74; read from GET
/v1/{family}/{id}); aiport, aiprocessor, doorlock and nvr have no official PATCH
and use the private PATCH /{collection}/{id} (nvr: PATCH /nvr, no device_id),
read from GET /doorlocks/{id} or the bootstrap. settings is sent as given (partial
nested objects too). The record is read first: when every leaf already matches,
nothing is sent and {status: "noop", reason, resource} is returned. Returns
otherwise {status: "updated", verified, before, after, response, _route}: verified
is true when the read-after carries every sent leaf (type-strict), null with
readAfterError when it cannot be read. An empty settings object fails before any
request. With dry-run policy, returns {status: "dry_run", before, response:
PREVIEW}. Dry-run response previews include body and params.

Required arguments: host, device_type, settings (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id from list_hosts (reportedState.hostname or name,
case-insensitive, or the long data[].id); for example "my-console".

device_type.description:
aiport, aiprocessor, bridge, camera, chime, doorlock, light,
linkstation, sensor, speaker, viewer or nvr; for example "chime".

settings.description:
Fields to change (free-form object, sent as given); for example
{"name": "Hallway chime"}.

device_id.description:

tools.name: upload_protect_file
tools.description:
Upload a Protect device asset file. WARNING: Uploads asset file to NVR storage.
Overwriting system files may not be reversible.

Consequence: the file is stored on the console and may overwrite an existing asset, which may
not be reversible.

Returns {status: "uploaded", response}: response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded
JSON, the text of a non-JSON body, or null when the body is empty).
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: {status: "dry_run", response (the preview)}.

`file_type`: Protect asset category. Protect 7.3.74 documents one value, 'animations';
  the value is passed through as given and selects the upload target path
  (/files/{file_type}). The category is not
  validated on read-back, so pass a known category exactly.

Request body: Protect 7.3.74 POST /v1/files/{fileType} is a multipart upload; the tool builds
the file part from filename + file_content_base64. No JSON body. The part's Content-Type is
content_type when given, else the spec type of the filename extension: .gif image/gif,
.jpg/.jpeg image/jpeg, .png image/png, .mp3 audio/mpeg, .m4a/.mp4 audio/mp4, .wav
audio/wave, .caf audio/x-caf. Any other extension without content_type is rejected before
any request, listing these types.

Example call (upload_protect_file):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "file_type": "animations",
      "filename": "alert.gif",
      "file_content_base64": "R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACw="
    }

body) and multipart: one {field, filename, contentType, sizeBytes} entry per file part

'animations'. Letters, digits, '-' and '_' only; anything else is rejected before
any request.

Filename for the uploaded asset; its extension selects the part's Content-Type
unless content_type is given.

file_content_base64.description:
File bytes, standard base64 (padded). Line-wrapped base64 (MIME/PEM
line breaks) is accepted; a data: URL prefix is not.

content_type.description:
Optional MIME type of the file part (e.g. "audio/wave"), sent as given; omit
it to derive the type from the filename extension.

when every site fails). incomplete/incompleteReason name any site resolved against a

tools.name: get_fleet_summary
tools.description:
Get a high-level fleet summary: host, site, and device counts with status breakdowns.

Useful for a quick overview of the entire UniFi deployment. Covers every
configured API key unless key_label names one (per-key failures under errors). A
console visible to more than one key is counted once, with its sites and devices,
under the first key in configuration order (as list_all_clients does).

Returns counts only, no records: {hosts, sites, devices: {total, byStatus, byType},
_key_label}, plus, when several keys are covered, _key_labels (the keys whose consoles
are counted) and _keyTotals (one entry per answering key label, each {hosts, sites,
devices: {total, byStatus, byType}} over the consoles counted under that key, so the
per-key numbers sum to the top-level totals; a shared console appears only under its
first key and a key that failed has no entry). errors lists a key that failed (its
label and reason), and incomplete/incompleteReason is added when a list stopped at
the opt-in UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap.

key_label.description:
Optional configured API-key label (see list_configured_api_keys). Omit to
cover every configured key: every key's consoles, sites and devices are counted
together, and a key that fails is reported under errors.
