tools.description:
Get details for a single UniFi console by name or ID.

Returns the upstream response object verbatim: the host record under data (including
reportedState GPS coordinates) beside httpStatusCode and traceId.

Required arguments: host (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id: the short name from list_hosts
(data[].reportedState.hostname or reportedState.name, case-insensitive, e.g.
"my-console") or the long data[].id (MAC:numericId composite).

tools.name: get_isp_metrics
tools.description:
Get WAN health metrics (speed, latency, packet loss, uptime).

`interval` ('5m' or '1h') is the metric bucket size. This is the unscoped variant (every
site the key sees); duration, or begin_timestamp/end_timestamp, bound the time range. To
scope by console/site, use `query_isp_metrics` instead.

Returns the upstream body verbatim: {data, httpStatusCode, traceId}. data is a list with
one object per site, {metricType, hostId, siteId, periods}; each periods[] entry is
{metricTime, version, data: {wan: {avgLatency, maxLatency, packetLoss, download_kbps,
upload_kbps, uptime, downtime, ispName, ispAsn}}}. So the WAN values of a site are at
data[i].periods[j].data.wan.

In a multi-key deployment every configured key is queried and the result keeps the same
data path: data holds every key's per-site objects (each with an additive _keyLabel),
byKey (one entry per key label) holds the rest of that key's body (httpStatusCode,
traceId), _key_labels lists the keys that answered, and a key that fails is reported
under errors.

interval.description: time bucket for metrics aggregation — '5m' or '1h'.

duration.description:
Optional (query duration): time range ending now — '24h' for 5m metrics, '7d'
or '30d' for 1h metrics. Cannot be combined with begin_timestamp/end_timestamp.

begin_timestamp.description:
Optional (query beginTimestamp): earliest time, an RFC3339 string such
as "2026-07-23T00:00:00Z".

end_timestamp.description: Optional (query endTimestamp): latest time, an RFC3339 string.

tools.name: get_sdwan_config
tools.description:
Get a single SD-WAN configuration by ID.

Returns the upstream response object verbatim: the configuration under data beside
httpStatusCode and traceId.
In a multi-key deployment every configured key is tried and the first that answers is used.

Example call (get_sdwan_config):
    {"config_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"}

config_id.description: SD-WAN configuration id (Site Manager). Get it from list_sdwan_configs (id).

tools.name: get_sdwan_config_status
tools.description:
Get the status of an SD-WAN configuration by ID.

Returns the upstream response object verbatim: the status under data beside
httpStatusCode and traceId.
In a multi-key deployment every configured key is tried and the first that answers is used.

Example call (get_sdwan_config_status):
    {"config_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6"}

config_id.description: SD-WAN configuration id (Site Manager). Get it from list_sdwan_configs (id).

tools.name: get_site_health_summary
tools.description:
Get a site's health: the Classic /stat/health body, verbatim.

Returns the controller's {meta, data} envelope unchanged: meta is {rc, msg?} and data has
one record per subsystem (wan, www, wlan, lan, vpn) with its status and that subsystem's
counters (e.g. num_adopted / num_disconnected devices, num_user clients, wan latency and
uptime fields), plus an additive _healthSummary {subsystems: {subsystem: status}, notOk:
[subsystem…], allOk} derived from data[] (omitted when data has no subsystem records). When
the site was resolved against a partial Site Manager site list the result adds _incomplete
and _incompleteReason.

site.description:
Site Manager site name or siteId (list_sites: data[].meta.desc / meta.name, or
siteId). A name shared by sites on several consoles is rejected with the matches
listed; pass that siteId then.

tools.name: get_site_inventory
tools.description:
Get full inventory for a site: all devices and connected clients.

_devicesEnvelope and _clientsEnvelope hold each list's upstream envelope fields (totalCount,
...).

Returns {_siteId (the console site UUID), _devices, _deviceCount, _clients, _clientCount}
(the two upstream record lists, verbatim, under additive keys); both
lists are drained across every page (incomplete=true with the reason only when the opt-in
UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap stops a drain).

site.description:
Site Manager site name or siteId (list_sites: data[].meta.desc / meta.name, or
siteId). A name shared by sites on several consoles is rejected with the matches
listed; pass that siteId then.

device_filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as
the `filter` query parameter of the site's device list. Omitted when unset.

client_filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as
the `filter` query parameter of the site's client list. Omitted when unset.

tools.name: list_all_clients
tools.description:
List all connected clients across all sites.

Returns {data, _count, _sitesQueried, _sitesSucceeded, _sitesFailed, _sitesIncomplete,
_key_label, _siteEnvelopes}: data holds every site's client records verbatim plus additive
_hostId / _hostName / _siteId / _siteName (and _keyLabel with several keys); _siteEnvelopes
maps "hostId/siteId" to that site list's upstream envelope fields (totalCount ...). errors,
_skipped, _key_labels and incomplete / incompleteReason are added when they apply.

Fans out requests to every site (of every configured API key unless key_label
names one; a console visible to more than one key is queried once, under the first key
in configuration order), drains each site's client list across all pages, and aggregates
results with source host/site annotations on each client record, under data (with
the additive _count). Reports the additive _sitesQueried, _sitesSucceeded,
_sitesFailed and _sitesIncomplete, per-site errors, and _skipped (hosts/sites that
could not be queried, each with its reason). A site whose client list stopped at the
UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap counts in _sitesIncomplete, not as failed, and the result
carries incomplete=true with the reasons.

key_label.description:
Optional configured API-key label (see list_configured_api_keys). Omit to
cover every configured key: results are merged, each record carries an additive
_keyLabel, and a key that fails is reported under errors.

filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as
each site's upstream `filter` query parameter. Omitted entirely when unset.
Example: `type.eq('WIRED')`.

tools.name: list_all_devices
tools.description:
List all devices across the entire fleet.

Returns {data, _count, _filter, _key_label}: data holds the unwrapped device records
verbatim plus additive _hostId / _hostName / _updatedAt; with one key the upstream envelope
fields (httpStatusCode, traceId) sit beside them, with several keys they are under byKey
with _key_labels. errors and incomplete / incompleteReason are added when they apply.

Aggregates devices from all consoles (every configured API key unless key_label
names one; per-key failures under errors): /v1/devices returns one wrapper per console,
which is unwrapped so data[] holds the device objects (each carrying the wrapper's
fields as additive _hostId / _hostName / _updatedAt naming its console); the additive
_count is the number of devices, _filter echoes status_filter and _key_label the
key_label argument (_key_labels lists the keys whose devices are included when several
keys are covered; a key that fails is under errors). A
console visible to more than one key is listed once, under the first key in
configuration order (as list_all_clients does).
Optionally filter by status
(e.g. 'offline', 'online', 'updating') to find problem devices quickly.
status_filter is applied LOCALLY by exact (case-insensitive) match against each
device's status/state. WARNING: an unrecognised value is NOT rejected — it matches
nothing and returns an EMPTY device list, so a typo (e.g. 'ofline') looks like a
healthy fleet with zero problem devices rather than an error. Omit status_filter to
get the full fleet, then read the real status values off the returned records.

status_filter.description:
Optional status to match LOCALLY (exact, case-insensitive) against each
device's status/state, e.g. 'offline', 'online', 'updating'. An unrecognised value
is not rejected: it matches nothing and returns an empty list. An empty or
whitespace value applies no filter.

key_label.description:
Optional configured API-key label (see list_configured_api_keys). Omit to
cover every configured key: results are merged, each record carries an additive
_keyLabel, and a key that fails is reported under errors.

host_ids.description:
Optional console ids (list_hosts data[].id, the long MAC:numericId form),
forwarded verbatim as the upstream hostIds[] query parameter to every covered key
(an empty list sends no hostIds[] parameter).
Shape: string[]

time.description:
Optional RFC3339 timestamp, forwarded verbatim as the upstream time query
parameter (the spec's "last processed timestamp of devices").

tools.name: list_all_sites_aggregated
tools.description:
List all sites with aggregated health stats from the /v1/sites/ API.

Result: {data, _count} plus the upstream envelope fields (httpStatusCode, traceId); with several
keys {data, _count, _key_labels, byKey} plus errors.

Returns sites merged with health summary: device counts, client counts,
alerts, and connectivity status in a single call. Every page is drained (multi-key:
every key, per-key failures under errors); a capped drain is flagged incomplete and is
never cached for name resolution.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description:
List all devices across the fleet with status, firmware, and model.

Returns {data, _count, _consoleCount} plus upstream envelope fields. data contains
console wrappers {hostId, hostName, devices: [...]}, unchanged; _count counts their
devices and _consoleCount counts wrappers. Null/missing/empty devices count as 0.

Default drains all pages in batches of 200. page_size gathers native pages until
the requested wrapper count or the end; the full final page can exceed the total; _pageSize
reports requested count, actual sent sizes per request, observed effective size
and returned count. page_token accepts native nextToken for one verbatim page,
or the opaque _continuation string preserving the physical size when the
requested total changes. Capped drains carry incomplete.

The host filters server-side to that console on its owning key. Without host,
key_label or paging, several keys are aggregated with _keyLabel per wrapper,
_key_labels, byKey envelopes and per-key errors. Paging without host needs
key_label when several keys exist; a single selected key is named in _key_labels.

host.description:
Optional console name or composite id from list_hosts; for example
"my-console" from reportedState.hostname or its data[].id. Names are case-insensitive.

page_token.description:
Raw nextToken string for one verbatim page, or the returned opaque
_continuation string preserving physical size when changing page_size.
Example: the token from the previous response.

time.description:
Optional RFC3339 last-processed timestamp, forwarded unchanged as time;
for example "2026-10-26T00:00:00Z". Omitted when unset.

page_size.description:
Requested wrapper count, gathered across effective pages.
Omit both paging arguments to drain all. Example: `100`.

key_label.description:
Configured API-key label from list_configured_api_keys; required
with paging and no host when several keys exist. Example: "primary".

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description:
List all UniFi consoles (hosts) with firmware, WAN IP, and status.

Returns {data: [host…], _count} with upstream envelope fields, including GPS
coordinates. data[].id is the long composite id; reportedState.hostname/name is
the short name. Either identifies host arguments case-insensitively; ambiguous
names return the matching consoles so the caller can choose an id.

Default drains all pages in batches of 200. page_size gathers native pages until
the requested host count or the end; the full final page can exceed the total; _pageSize reports
requested count, actual sent sizes per request,
observed effective size and returned count. page_token accepts the unchanged
native nextToken for one verbatim page, or the opaque _continuation string
preserving its physical size when the requested total changes.
Capped drains carry incomplete=true.

With several keys, the default aggregates all keys, annotates each host with
_keyLabel, and returns _key_labels, byKey envelopes and per-key errors. key_label
reads one key and adds _key_labels. Paging with several keys needs key_label.

page_token.description:
Raw nextToken string for one verbatim page, or the returned opaque
_continuation string preserving physical size when changing page_size.
Example: the token from the previous response.

page_size.description:
Requested host count, gathered across effective pages. Omit both
paging arguments to drain every page. Example: `100`.

key_label.description:
Configured API-key label from list_configured_api_keys to read one
key; required with paging when several keys exist. Example: "primary".

tools.name: list_sdwan_configs
tools.description:
List Site Magic (SD-WAN) VPN mesh configurations.

Returns {data, _count} plus the upstream envelope fields (httpStatusCode, traceId), and
nextToken when the service returns one; with several keys {data, _count, _key_labels, byKey}
plus errors; incomplete / incompleteReason on a capped drain.

In a multi-key deployment without key_label every configured key is queried: results are
merged, each record carries an additive _keyLabel, and a key that fails is reported under
errors.

The published contract declares no pagination parameters or nextToken. By default the server
follows a nextToken if the service returns one. Pass page_token to fetch a single page manually;
with several API keys it needs key_label (a cursor belongs to one key's listing). A capped
drain returns the configs gathered so far with incomplete=true rather than truncating silently.

page_token.description:
Optional pagination cursor (a nextToken if returned by the service) to fetch one
page manually. Omit it to drain every page and get the complete list.
Example: the `nextToken` string from a previous response, passed unchanged.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description:
List all sites with device/client counts and ISP info.

Returns {data: [site...], _count} plus upstream envelope fields. siteId is the
Site Manager Fabric ObjectId, distinct from per-site proxy UUIDs. Pass site names
such as "Default" to tools; the server resolves the appropriate id.

Default drains all pages in batches of 200. page_size gathers native pages until
the requested site count or the end; the full final page can exceed the total; _pageSize reports
requested count, actual sent sizes per request,
observed effective size and returned count. page_token accepts the unchanged
native nextToken for one verbatim page, or the opaque _continuation string
preserving its physical size when the requested total changes.
Capped drains carry incomplete=true.

With several keys, the default aggregates all keys, annotates each site with
_keyLabel, and returns _key_labels, byKey envelopes and per-key errors. key_label
reads one key and adds _key_labels. Paging with several keys needs key_label.

page_token.description:
Raw nextToken string for one verbatim page, or the returned opaque
_continuation string preserving physical size when changing page_size.
Example: the token from the previous response.

page_size.description:
Requested site count, gathered across effective pages. Omit both
paging arguments to drain every page. Example: `100`.

key_label.description:
Configured API-key label from list_configured_api_keys to read one
key; required with paging when several keys exist. Example: "primary".

tools.name: query_isp_metrics
tools.description:
Query filtered ISP metrics for one or more scoped sites (via `sites`, or `host`+`site`).

One of: `sites`, or `host`+`site` (passing both is an error, never a duplicate query).

This is the filtered variant of `get_isp_metrics`: pass host/site to scope the query and
start_time/end_time to bound the window. For a quick unscoped read, use `get_isp_metrics`.

Returns the upstream body verbatim: {data: {metrics, status?, message?}, httpStatusCode,
traceId}. data.metrics has one object per site, {metricType, hostId, siteId, periods};
each periods[] entry is {metricTime, version, data: {wan: {...}}}. data.status /
data.message report a partial success (some sites returned no data).

In a multi-key deployment each site is queried on the key that owns its console. When
the sites span several keys the result keeps the same data.metrics path: it holds every
key's per-site objects (each with an additive _keyLabel), byKey (one entry per key
label) holds the rest of that key's body verbatim (its data.status / data.message,
httpStatusCode, traceId),
_key_labels lists the keys that answered, and a key whose query fails is reported under
errors (the call fails only when every key fails).

Required arguments: interval (see each parameter's description).

interval.description: time bucket for metrics aggregation — '5m' or '1h'.

host.description:
Optional. Console name or id: the short name from list_hosts
(data[].reportedState.hostname or reportedState.name, case-insensitive, e.g.
"my-console") or the long data[].id (MAC:numericId composite). One console serves both
Network and Protect. Resolves to hostId.

site.description: site name or ID — resolves to siteId automatically.

sites.description:
advanced use — list of {hostId, siteId} dicts, optionally with per-entry
beginTimestamp/endTimestamp. hostId may be a console name or id (resolved to the
id); siteId must be a Site Manager site on that console (from list_sites; a site
name is resolved too). An unknown console or site fails before the query, listing
the valid choices; a malformed hostId/siteId (empty, whitespace, control character)
fails before any request. A null beginTimestamp/endTimestamp is treated as absent
(start_time/end_time apply). Use host/site instead for a single site. An empty list
names no site: with host/site those scope the query; alone it is sent as given
({"sites": []}) for the upstream to judge, and an upstream error gets a hint
appended.
Shape: ({hostId:string,siteId:string,beginTimestamp?:string|null,
endTimestamp?:string|null}|null)[]

start_time.description:
ISO 8601 UTC timestamp STRINGS, e.g. "2026-07-23T00:00:00Z". These are strings,
NOT epoch numbers — passing an epoch integer (seconds or milliseconds) is rejected by
schema validation with 'Input should be a valid string [type=string_type]'. (Note the
deliberate inconsistency with the epoch-based history tools: list_protect_events,
list_client_sessions and get_historical_stats take epoch SECONDS as integers, whereas
this Site Manager tool takes ISO 8601 strings.) An epoch supplied AS a string (e.g.
"1690000000000") is also rejected, with the expected format, rather than being forwarded
to the API as a meaningless window. An empty or
whitespace-only value is an error, never read as omitted.

end_time.description:
ISO 8601 UTC timestamp STRINGS, e.g. "2026-07-23T00:00:00Z". These are strings,
NOT epoch numbers — passing an epoch integer (seconds or milliseconds) is rejected by
schema validation with 'Input should be a valid string [type=string_type]'. (Note the
deliberate inconsistency with the epoch-based history tools: list_protect_events,
list_client_sessions and get_historical_stats take epoch SECONDS as integers, whereas
this Site Manager tool takes ISO 8601 strings.) An epoch supplied AS a string (e.g.
"1690000000000") is also rejected, with the expected format, rather than being forwarded
to the API as a meaningless window. An empty or
whitespace-only value is an error, never read as omitted.

tools.name: search_across_sites
tools.description:
Search for devices or clients matching a query across all sites.

Returns {data (the matching records), _count, _query, _sitesTotal, _sitesSearched,
_sitesSucceeded, _sitesFailed, _sitesIncomplete} plus errors and _skipped (sites that could
not be searched, each with its reason) when present. Each errors entry is an object {key
(the API-key label), siteId, scope ("devices" / "clients" for a per-site fetch failure;
"sites" with siteId "" for a key whose site list failed), reason (a string)}. A site whose
device or client list stopped at
the UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap counts in _sitesIncomplete (not _sitesFailed or
_sitesSucceeded) and the result carries
incomplete=true with the reasons. Each match is the upstream record plus additive _type /
_siteId / _siteName / _hostId (its console), and _keyLabel (the API key that read it) when
several keys are configured.

query.description:
case-insensitive substring matched against a device's name, macAddress,
ipAddress or model, or a client's name, macAddress, ipAddress or hostname, e.g.
"02:00:5e" or "10.0.2.". An empty or whitespace query applies no filter: every
device and client record of every searched site is returned.

tools.name: search_device_fleet
tools.description:
Search for a device by name, MAC address, or model across the entire fleet.

Result: {data, _count, _query, _key_label}: _query and _key_label echo the arguments.

Returns all matching devices from all consoles (every configured API key unless
key_label names one; per-key failures under errors); each match carries the wrapper's
fields as additive _hostId / _hostName / _updatedAt naming its console. A console
visible to more than one key is searched once, under the first key in configuration
order.

Required arguments: query (see each parameter's description).

query.description:
REQUIRED. Search string matched against device name, model, and MAC across the
fleet. An empty or whitespace query applies no filter: every device is returned.

key_label.description:
Optional configured API-key label (see list_configured_api_keys). Omit to
cover every configured key: results are merged, each record carries an additive
_keyLabel, and a key that fails is reported under errors.

tools.name: get_client_link_diagnostics
tools.description:
Get first-class per-client link/policy diagnostics for one or more clients.

Read-only and Fabric-only: reuses the same Classic REST
/v1/connector/consoles/{host_id}/proxy/network/api/s/{site_slug}/stat/sta request as
list_active_clients_stats, then selects the requested client(s) from that payload in
memory. Surfaces link quality (rssi, signal, noise, channel, radio_name),
rx_rate/tx_rate and retry counters, satisfaction_reason, network/VLAN identity, QoS,
fixed-IP, and virtual-network override fields when upstream provides them — the
matching record is returned unchanged, so unknown/future fields survive.

Returns: the /stat/sta envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [client…]} with data narrowed to the
selected client(s), in the requested order (one entry for client_id).

`client_id`: a single client selector — the client's MAC address (case- and
  separator-insensitive) or its classic /stat/sta _id. The Integration API client id
  from list_clients data[].id does not match. Provide EITHER client_id OR client_ids,
  not both.
`client_ids`: an explicit list of client selectors (any length) for multi-client
  selection, from one /stat/sta read. A selector that matches no client fails listing
  every valid client (name, mac, _id) rather than being silently skipped.

Example call (get_client_link_diagnostics):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "client_id": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

client_id.description:
Single client MAC address or classic /stat/sta _id. Pass this OR
client_ids, not both. The MAC is matched case- and separator-insensitively:
macAddress from list_clients, or mac from list_active_clients_stats. The _id is
the _id from list_active_clients_stats. The Integration API client id
(list_clients data[].id, as used by get_client) is a different identifier and
does not match.

client_ids.description:
Client selectors (any number), each a MAC address or classic /stat/sta
_id (same sources as client_id). Pass this OR client_id, not both. An empty
list applies no filter: the whole /stat/sta envelope is returned verbatim (with
client_id also given, client_id selects).
Shape: string[]

tools.name: get_device_port_state
tools.description:
Get switch port health, PoE, optics, and LLDP telemetry for a device.

Returns, for the device view, an object with the keys _device, _port_idx (null),
_source, _thermal_power and _device_record, plus port_table and lldp_table only when the
selected record has them and meta only when the upstream envelope has it; with port_idx,
_device, _port_idx, _source and _port, plus meta only when the envelope has it. An
absent table or meta is left out, never returned as null. meta, port_table, lldp_table
and the _device_record / _port rows are upstream values verbatim; _device / _port_idx
echo the arguments, _source names the read route (/stat/device) and _thermal_power is a
summary of the record's thermal and power fields (only those it has; {} when none).

Read-only and Fabric-only: reuses the same Classic REST
/v1/connector/consoles/{host_id}/proxy/network/api/s/{site_slug}/stat/device request
as list_device_stats (one call, no new route), then projects the selected device's
port telemetry from that payload. Upstream operational fields are preserved
verbatim — link state/speed/duplex, rx/tx byte/packet/error/drop counters, PoE state
and draw (poe_enable/poe_good/poe_power/poe_voltage/poe_current/poe_class/poe_mode),
SFP/optics fields where present, and port config identity — nothing is renamed or
dropped.

`port_idx`: optional port_table[].port_idx (ports count from 1; any non-negative
  value, 0 included, is matched as given). Omit it for the device view
  (port_table and lldp_table verbatim when the record has them, a thermal/power
  summary, and the complete selected /stat/device record verbatim under
  _device_record); set it to return that single port_table row verbatim (under _port).
  An unknown port_idx fails listing the valid port_idx values.
  Both views carry the upstream envelope's meta verbatim when it has one; an unknown
  device fails listing every valid device (name, mac, _id).

Example call (get_device_port_state):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "device_id": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

device_id.description:
Device MAC address or classic /stat/device _id. The MAC is matched case- and
separator-insensitively: macAddress from list_site_devices, mac from list_devices
or list_device_stats. The _id is the _id from list_device_stats. The Integration
API device id (list_site_devices data[].id, as used by get_device) is a different
identifier and does not match.

port_idx.description:
Optional port_table[].port_idx (switch ports count from 1; any non-negative
value, 0 included, is matched as given); omit for the whole device view.

tools.name: get_device_stp_state
tools.description:
Get per-device STP/RSTP state and per-port STP role/state/path-cost.

The result's top-level keys are {meta, _device, _source, _stp, _ports, _device_record}:
_device echoes the device_id argument and _source names the read route (/stat/device).

Read-only and Fabric-only: reads the same Classic REST
/v1/connector/consoles/{host_id}/proxy/network/api/s/{site_slug}/stat/device payload
as list_device_stats and projects the selected device's STP fields. Returns the
device-level stp_version, stp_priority, root_switch/root (and any other stp_* field
present) plus per-port STP role/state/path-cost where upstream provides them, all
verbatim (under _stp and _ports), the complete selected /stat/device record verbatim
under _device_record, and
the upstream envelope's meta verbatim. An unknown device fails listing every valid
device (name, mac, _id). This tool is read-only: no write is performed.

Example call (get_device_stp_state):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "device_id": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

device_id.description:
Device MAC address or classic /stat/device _id. The MAC is matched case- and
separator-insensitively: macAddress from list_site_devices, mac from list_devices
or list_device_stats. The _id is the _id from list_device_stats. The Integration
API device id (list_site_devices data[].id, as used by get_device) is a different
identifier and does not match.

tools.name: get_historical_stats
tools.description:
Get bucketed historical statistics from the Classic REST /stat/report endpoint.

Output "time" is epoch milliseconds. Note: rx_bytes/tx_bytes come back as JSON
floats in scientific notation (e.g. 5.27e9) — treat them as floats, not ints.

Returns the Classic REST envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [bucket…]} verbatim.

An empty data array means the controller has no report rows, not a malformed request:
Network 11.x controllers (verified on 11.0.81) answer every /stat/report request —
each interval and scope, with or without attrs/start/end — with
{"meta": {"rc": "ok"}, "data": []}, while sibling stat routes such as /stat/session
still return rows. On those releases the dashboard history is served by the v2
aggregated dashboard; read it with fabric_connector_get, path
"network/v2/api/site/{site}/aggregated-dashboard".

Required arguments: host, site, interval, scope, start, end (see each parameter's
description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

interval.description:
one of "minute", "5minutes", "hourly", "daily", "monthly", "archive" (every
interval the controller accepts; another value fails listing these).

scope.description:
one of "site", "ap", "user", "gw", "sw", "device", "speedtest", "isp" (every
scope the controller accepts; another value fails listing these). The "ap" scope
carries num_sta per AP per bucket.

start.description:
epoch SECONDS (UTC). Unlike /stat/session, this endpoint requires MILLISECONDS —
the tool converts seconds to milliseconds internally, so callers always pass seconds
for a consistent interface.

end.description:
epoch SECONDS (UTC). Unlike /stat/session, this endpoint requires MILLISECONDS —
the tool converts seconds to milliseconds internally, so callers always pass seconds
for a consistent interface.

attrs.description:
optional report metrics to aggregate, e.g. ["num_sta", "rx_bytes",
"tx_bytes"]. Sent as the request's attrs exactly as given; when omitted no attrs
key is sent and the controller decides which fields each bucket carries.
Shape: string[]

tools.name: get_scoped_system_log
tools.description:
Read the Network system log for one device, client connection, admin-activity record
or external id (a plain GET, no drain).

GET network/v2/api/site/{site}/system-log/{scope}/{identifier}, returned verbatim.
scope selects the route: "device" (identifier is a device MAC address; HTTP 200 with a
list of events on a live console, probed 2026-10-17), "client-connection" (identifier
is a client MAC address; HTTP 200 on a live console but the one client tried returned
an empty list, so the entry shape is unproven), "admin-activity" (identifier is an
admin-activity record id) and "by-external-id" (identifier is an external id). The last
two answered HTTP 404 on the probe console for an id it did not hold (it had no admin
record and no external-id match), so their positive responses have not been observed.
The routes come from the Network 11.0.81 web app; no published schema describes the
responses. For a whole class (all, device-alert, ...) use get_system_log or
list_network_events. An unknown scope fails before any request listing the choices.

Returns the upstream body verbatim (a list of events for device; nonobjects use
result).

Example call (get_scoped_system_log):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "scope": "device",
      "identifier": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

scope.description:
Which log to read: "device", "client-connection", "admin-activity" or
"by-external-id". Example: `device`.

identifier.description:
The id the scope names: a device MAC (device), a client MAC
(client-connection), an admin-activity record id or an external id. Sent as one
URL path segment. Example: `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`.

query.description:
Optional query-string parameters sent as given (the web app builds a dynamic
query for the device and client-connection routes; its keys are not published).
Free-form JSON object; omit for none. Example: `{}`.

tools.name: get_site_statistics
tools.description:
Get site health statistics: latency, throughput, and client counts per subsystem.

Returns the Classic REST /stat/health envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [subsystem health…]}
verbatim, plus an additive _healthSummary {subsystems: {subsystem: status}, notOk:
[subsystem…], allOk} derived from data[] (omitted when data has no subsystem records).

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

tools.name: get_system_info
tools.description:
Get controller/console system info: version, uptime, and memory.

Returns the Classic REST /stat/sysinfo envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [system info…]}
verbatim.

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

tools.name: get_system_log
tools.description:
Read Network system-log events and alerts.

POST network/v2/api/site/{site}/system-log/{log_class} with the supplied query body
(classified as a write; Consequence: none intended, it only reads).
Classes seen on Network 11.0.81: all, device-alert, client-alert, admin-activity,
update-alert, threat-alert (IPS/IDS), next-ai-alert, vpn-alert, critical; triggers
answered 404. Any other class is sent as given.
Class filter keys default to the entry kinds the controller UI sends
(nextAiCategory, activity_keys, change_keys, systemLogDeviceTypes, clientType,
guestAuthorizationMethod, threatTypes, triggerTypes); query_body can override them.

UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny or family:network=deny hides this tool before requests
(not read-POST allowlisted). dry-run policy previews the first page without sending:
{status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params,
body}}.

Returns, by default, every page drained into {data: [entry, ...], total_element_count,
incomplete?, incompleteReason?}. Entries are verbatim; the count is the first
page's. Caps, repeated entries, early empty pages or short totals mark the result
incomplete; an object with unprovable pagination raises (request an explicit page
to inspect it). A scalar response is returned verbatim. With page alone, returns
{data, page_number, total_element_count, total_page_count} verbatim; critical normally
returns a bare array. page_size alone is window 0; resume with page=_nextPage and
the same page_size. With page, the window (see page). _pageSize: requested, sent
(each pageSize sent, in order), effective, returned. No _nextPage: nothing follows
the window, or the call stopped incomplete.
Narrow large logs with timestampFrom/timestampTo in query_body.
Each page is sent once; HTTP 429 stops the call (narrow or use page).

Example call (get_system_log):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "log_class": "client-alert",
      "query_body": {"timestampFrom": 1760140800000, "timestampTo": 1760227200000}
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

log_class.description:
The log class (URL path segment), e.g. "all", "device-alert",
"client-alert", "admin-activity", "update-alert", "threat-alert",
"next-ai-alert", "vpn-alert", "critical". Default "all".

query_body.description:
Optional query body sent as given: a time window in epoch milliseconds
(timestampFrom, timestampTo) or a class's own filter keys such as threatTypes. A
pageNumber / pageSize in it is honoured like page / page_size (the arguments win
when both are given).
Example: `{"timestampFrom": 1760140800000, "timestampTo": 1760227200000}`.
Free-form JSON object; no fixed body shape is published.

page.description:
Zero-based page. With page_size, returns exactly page_size records starting
at record page * page_size, gathered across console pages whatever the console
page size; resume with _nextPage and the same page_size. Without page_size, one
request returns that console page verbatim. Example: `2`.

page_size.description:
Optional entry count (sent as pageSize): alone, window 0 (the first
page_size entries, fewer only at the end); with page, the window size. Omit to
drain all in batches of 1000. Example: `100`.

tools.name: list_active_clients_stats
tools.description:
List detailed per-client statistics: traffic, signal strength, and experience score.

Returns the Classic REST /stat/sta envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [client stats…]}
verbatim.

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

tools.name: list_client_sessions
tools.description:
List historical client connection sessions from the Classic REST /stat/session endpoint.

This is the highest-value history tool: retention is ~90 days, so it covers
far more than the currently-connected client list.

Each session includes mac, is_wired, assoc_time (session start, epoch seconds),
duration (seconds), ap_mac, rx_bytes, tx_bytes, satisfaction, hostname, ip, _id, and
roaming_sessions[]. Two things that surprise callers:
- There is NO explicit disconnect timestamp — session end is assoc_time + duration.
- Radio band lives ONLY inside roaming_sessions[] (radio_band: na/ng/6e), never at the
  top level. Wired sessions have ap_mac=null and carry sw_mac/sw_port instead.

Returns the Classic REST envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [session…]} verbatim, including
identifiers (MAC/IP/hostname).

Required arguments: host, site, start, end (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

start.description:
epoch SECONDS (UTC). This endpoint uses seconds natively — passing milliseconds
returns HTTP 200 with an EMPTY array and no error. A negative or
millisecond-magnitude value (>= 1e11) is sent as given and the result carries a
_warnings entry saying so.

end.description:
epoch SECONDS (UTC). This endpoint uses seconds natively — passing milliseconds
returns HTTP 200 with an EMPTY array and no error. A negative or
millisecond-magnitude value (>= 1e11) is sent as given and the result carries a
_warnings entry saying so.

session_type.description:
session class filter. The values that actually narrow the result are "all"
(default — the full unfiltered set), "user" (regular clients), and "guest"
(guest-network clients). Valid values: "all", "user", "guest", "voucher"; any
other value fails before any request, listing them (the endpoint itself ignores an
unknown value and returns the full "all" set, so a typo would otherwise yield
everything). (UniFi documents "voucher" as a fourth class; on tested firmware it
returned the full set, so prefer "user"/"guest" for real narrowing.)

tools.name: list_controller_stat_schemas
tools.description:
List schemas supported by a controller's Network 11.x statistics engine.

GET /v2/api/stats/schemas through the selected console. Each upstream schema can
describe its name, keys, values, and nested groups. Returns the upstream body verbatim;
FastMCP wraps an array in result for MCP clients.
Network versions without the modern statistics engine may return an upstream 404.

Required argument: host (see the parameter description).

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

tools.name: list_device_stats
tools.description:
List per-device statistics: CPU load, memory, uptime, and port throughput.

Returns the Classic REST /stat/device envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [device stats…]}
verbatim.

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

tools.name: list_ips_events
tools.description:
List intrusion prevention / detection (IPS/IDS) threat events, every page drained.

Network 11.x reports IPS events in the system log's threat-alert class (the Classic
stat/ips/event route answers HTTP 404 on Network 11.0.81). This reads POST
network/v2/api/site/{site}/system-log/threat-alert (classified as a write;
Consequence: none intended, it only reads the log) with
threatTypes (default
["HONEYPOT", "THREAT"], what the controller UI sends; without it the controller returns
no entries) and timestampFrom / timestampTo from start / end when given.

These POST queries are treated as writes pending a separately approved read-POST
allowlist PR. UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny and family:network=deny hide the tool
before any upstream request.
dry-run policy returns {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}} for the first page without sending a POST.

Returns {data: [event, ...], total_element_count, incomplete?, incompleteReason?}: each
event verbatim (key such as THREAT_DETECTED_KNOWN_SOURCE_CLIENT, category SECURITY,
severity, timestamp in epoch ms, parameters with the signature, source and destination,
...); incomplete / incompleteReason appear when the opt-in UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap,
repeated entries, an early empty page, or a short declared total stopped the drain.
Unprovable pagination metadata raises a clear error; use get_system_log with an explicit
page to inspect it. _warnings flags a negative or millisecond-like start / end
(still multiplied by 1000). Without start / end the whole retained log is read.

Example call (list_ips_events):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "start": 1760140800
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

start.description:
Optional window start, epoch seconds (sent as timestampFrom in milliseconds).
Example: `1760140800`.

end.description:
Optional window end, epoch seconds (sent as timestampTo in milliseconds).
Example: `1760227200`.

tools.name: list_known_clients
tools.description:
List the full per-site client roster incl. offline history (Classic REST /stat/alluser).

Unlike list_active_clients_stats (currently-connected only), this includes clients
seen historically — typically far more entries. (Distinct from the fleet-wide
list_all_clients aggregation tool, which spans every console.) This endpoint accepts GET.

Each entry includes mac, first_seen, last_seen, disconnect_timestamp (all epoch
seconds), is_wired, oui, last_ip, last_radio, hostname, and device-fingerprint fields.

Returns the Classic REST envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [client…]} verbatim, including
identifiers (MAC/IP/hostname/name). With source "v2" (or any of the v2
arguments) the controller's v2 client history (GET
network/v2/api/site/{site}/clients/history, the web UI's route) is returned verbatim
instead; Classic stays the default because the v2 rows lack name, note, fixed_ip,
network_id, local_dns_record, virtual_network_override_id and disconnect_timestamp.

Required arguments: host, site (see each parameter's description).

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

source.description:
Optional route: "classic" (default, /stat/alluser) or "v2". Every
other argument below applies only to "v2" and selects it.
Example: `v2`.

within_hours.description:
Optional v2 query withinHours: clients seen in the last N hours,
sent as given. Example: `24`.

only_blocked.description:
Optional v2 query onlyBlocked: true lists blocked clients only.
Example: `true`.

only_non_blocked.description:
Optional v2 query onlyNonBlocked: true lists non-blocked clients
only. Example: `true`.

include_matter_thread_clients.description:
Optional v2 query includeMatterThreadClients: true
also lists Matter/Thread clients. Example: `true`.

include_traffic_usage.description:
Optional v2 query includeTrafficUsage: true asks the
controller to include traffic usage. Example: `true`.

include_unifi_devices.description:
Optional v2 query includeUnifiDevices: true asks the
controller to include UniFi devices. Example: `false`.

tools.name: list_network_events
tools.description:
List site network events from the system log, draining every page in controller order.

Network 11.x keeps events in the system log (the Classic stat/event route answers
HTTP 404 on Network 11.0.81). This reads class "all" of POST
network/v2/api/site/{site}/system-log/all (classified as a write), with
timestampFrom / timestampTo
set from start / end when given. view reads another class the same way (live on
Network 11.0.81: all, device-alert, client-alert, admin-activity, update-alert,
threat-alert, next-ai-alert, vpn-alert, critical). vpn_user_id scopes the log to one VPN
user instead: GET network/v2/api/site/{site}/system-log/vpn-user-connection?vpnUserId=
(the web UI's route), returned verbatim. For a raw query use get_system_log.

Consequence: none intended. Read POSTs are classed as writes (not read-POST
allowlisted). UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny or family:network=deny hides the whole tool.
dry-run policy previews the first page without sending a POST:
{status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message,
preview: {method, path, params, body}}.

Returns {data: [event, ...], total_element_count, incomplete?, incompleteReason?}:
each event verbatim (key such as CLIENT_ROAMED_2 or THREAT_DETECTED_KNOWN_SOURCE_CLIENT,
category, severity, timestamp in epoch ms, parameters, ...); total_element_count is the
controller's count; incomplete / incompleteReason appear when the opt-in
UNIFI_PAGINATE_MAX_PAGES cap, repeated entries, an early empty page, or a short declared
total stopped the drain. Unprovable pagination metadata raises a clear error; use
get_system_log with an explicit page to inspect it. _warnings flags a negative or
millisecond-like start / end (still multiplied by 1000; _warnings includes sent_as).
Without start / end the whole retained log is read (tens of thousands of entries
on a busy site).

Example call (list_network_events):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "start": 1760140800,
      "end": 1760227200
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

start.description:
Optional window start, epoch seconds (sent as timestampFrom in milliseconds).
Example: `1760140800`.

end.description:
Optional window end, epoch seconds (sent as timestampTo in milliseconds).
Example: `1760227200`.

view.description:
Optional system-log class to read instead of "all" (URL path segment, sent
as given), e.g. "device-alert" or "admin-activity". Default "all".
Example: `device-alert`.

vpn_user_id.description:
Optional VPN user id: reads that user's VPN connection log (query
vpnUserId, a GET) instead of a class; start, end and view do not apply.
Example: `000000000000000000000107`.

tools.name: list_speedtest_results
tools.description:
List archived WAN speed-test results for a site and time window.

Reads the private Classic REST POST /stat/report/archive.speedtest route. It
requests download/upload throughput, latency, result time, interface name and WAN
network group. Network 11 may keep its current history on a newer private v2 route;
an empty archive is returned unchanged.

Returns the controller's complete response body verbatim. No fields are filtered,
masked, projected or truncated.

Required arguments: host, site, start, end (see each parameter's description).

host.description:
Console name or id: the short name from list_hosts
(data[].reportedState.hostname or reportedState.name, case-insensitive,
e.g. "my-console") or the long data[].id (MAC:numericId composite).

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from
list_local_sites (name or id). Names like "Default" work.

start.description:
Inclusive window start as an integer epoch-seconds timestamp. The tool
converts it to the route's required epoch milliseconds.

end.description:
Inclusive window end as an integer epoch-seconds timestamp. The tool
converts it to the route's required epoch milliseconds.

tools.name: control_site_vpn
tools.description:
Enable, disable or rebuild a site VPN (Classic POST cmd/sitemgr).

Consequence: disable and rebuild interrupt traffic between the sites.
Required: host, site and action. Sends cmd enable-site-vpn, disable-site-vpn or
rebuild-site-vpn with name and site (vpn_site) when given (the web app's
enable/disable body) plus any free-form params (rebuild has no captured body).
Success requires meta.rc ok; any other answer raises with the full upstream body.
Returns the Classic {meta, data} envelope verbatim. Dry-run (dry-run policy) returns
a dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}}; nothing is sent.

Example call (control_site_vpn):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "action": "disable",
     "name": "branch-vpn", "vpn_site": "branch-1"}

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or UUID, e.g. "Default".

action.description: One of enable, disable, rebuild, e.g. "disable".

vpn_site.description: The peer site sent as the body's site, e.g. "branch-1".

confirm.description: Ignored; accepted for compatibility. The call executes when made.

tools.name: create_radius_profile
tools.description:
Create a RADIUS authentication profile.

Uses Classic REST POST /proxy/network/api/s/{site}/rest/radiusprofile (the route the
controller's own UI uses; the published Integration API serves RADIUS profiles GET-only,
POST answers HTTP 405 on Network 11.0.81). The body is `fields` plus name, auth_servers
[{ip, port, x_secret}] and, when acct_server_ip is given, acct_servers [{ip, port,
x_secret}] carrying port and secret only when given. No port or flag is defaulted:
accounting stays off unless `fields` sets accounting_enabled.

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, the Classic envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [the created
radiusprofile record]}; data[].external_id is the id list_radius_profiles reports.
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status:
"dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

Example call (create_radius_profile):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "name": "Corp RADIUS",
      "auth_server_ip": "192.0.2.20",
      "auth_server_port": 1812,
      "auth_server_secret": "s3cret"
    }

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

name.description: Display name for the RADIUS profile.

auth_server_ip.description: RADIUS authentication server IP address, e.g. 192.0.2.20.

auth_server_secret.description: Shared secret for the authentication server.

acct_server_ip.description: Optional accounting server IP address; adds an acct_servers entry.

acct_server_port.description:
Optional accounting UDP port (e.g. 1813); omitted when unset. It
belongs with acct_server_ip: without one, the acct_servers entry is sent without
ip as given, and an upstream error gets a hint.

acct_server_secret.description:
Optional accounting shared secret; belongs with acct_server_ip
(sent as given without one; an upstream error then gets a hint).

fields.description:
Optional further native radiusprofile keys merged into the body, e.g.
accounting_enabled, interim_update_enabled, vlan_enabled; name and the server
lists built from the arguments take precedence.
Free-form JSON object; no fixed body shape is published.

tools.name: create_site_to_site_tunnel
tools.description:
Create a site-to-site VPN tunnel. This is a write operation that modifies live config.

A manual site-to-site tunnel is a Classic REST networkconf record of purpose site-vpn,
written with POST /proxy/network/api/s/{site}/rest/networkconf (the route the
controller's own UI uses; the published Integration API serves site-to-site tunnels
GET-only, POST answers HTTP 405 on Network 11.0.81). The body is the controller's native
networkconf fields, sent verbatim with purpose set to site-vpn; pass name and vpn_type
(vpn_type values: ipsec-vpn (manual IPsec), openvpn-vpn, wireguard-vpn). The body is
sent as given and the controller validates the record: it answers
api.err.InvalidPayload when a field the tunnel type needs is missing, and that error
gets a hint naming the missing name / vpn_type.

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, the Classic envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [the created
networkconf record]}; data[].external_id is the id list_site_to_site_tunnels reports.
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status:
"dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

Example call (create_site_to_site_tunnel):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "tunnel": {
        "name": "Branch office",
        "vpn_type": "openvpn-vpn",
        "enabled": false,

tools.name: create_vpn_client
tools.description:
Create a VPN client connection on the gateway (WireGuard, OpenVPN or PPTP).

Consequence: an enabled VPN client makes the gateway connect to the peer, and
vpn_client_default_route true sends routed traffic through the tunnel; create it with
enabled false to review it first.

A VPN client is a Classic REST networkconf record of purpose vpn-client, written with
POST network/api/s/{site}/rest/networkconf (the route the controller's own UI uses).
The body is `fields` plus purpose, name and vpn_type, and enabled only when given;
nothing else is defaulted. The controller validates the record: a manual WireGuard
client needs wireguard_client_mode "manual", wireguard_client_peer_ip / _peer_port /
_peer_public_key, x_wireguard_private_key, ip_subnet and an interface DNS server
(dhcpd_dns_enabled true with dhcpd_dns_1), and answers
api.err.WireguardMissingInterfaceDns without the DNS server (verified on Network
11.0.81). An upstream error gets a hint listing those fields.

Returns the upstream Classic body verbatim: {meta: {rc}, data: [the created networkconf
record]} (under dry-run policy, the dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent:
false, message, preview: {method, path, params (query parameters), body}} instead).

Example call (create_vpn_client):
    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "name": "Office tunnel",
      "vpn_type": "wireguard",
      "enabled": false,
      "fields": {
        "wireguard_client_mode": "manual",
        "wireguard_client_peer_ip": "203.0.113.7",
        "wireguard_client_peer_port": 51820,
        "wireguard_client_peer_public_key": "PEER_PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64",
        "x_wireguard_private_key": "OWN_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64",
        "ip_subnet": "10.8.0.2/32",
        "dhcpd_dns_enabled": true,
        "dhcpd_dns_1": "10.8.0.1"
      }
    }

tools.name: list_radius_profiles
tools.description:
List RADIUS profiles for a site.

Returns {data, totalCount}: every page is drained; data holds the RADIUS profile records
verbatim and totalCount is the upstream total (null when none was reported). The first page's
other envelope fields are kept beside them, and incomplete / incompleteReason are added when a
capped drain stopped short.

RADIUS profiles are offset-paginated (native default page size 25); by default
every page is drained and the complete list is returned as {data, totalCount}.
Pass offset alone for a single manual page. A capped drain is flagged incomplete.

The limit requests a total, gathered automatically in batches up to 200;
_pageSize reports requested count, actual sent sizes per request,
observed effective size and returned count, without capping the total.

Required arguments: host, site.

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites (name or
id). Names like "Default" work.

offset.description:
Optional zero-based starting record; alone, fetch one page manually.
Example: `25`.

limit.description:
Without offset, the record count gathered from the start in pages of at
most 200; fewer only when the collection ends. With offset, limit is sent
unchanged as one page. The console clamps that page to 200, so fewer can
return while more exist (compare _pageSize requested and returned). Omit
offset and limit to drain all.
Example: `25`.

filter.description:
Optional Network Integration API filter expression, forwarded unchanged as the
upstream `filter` query parameter for server-side filtering (e.g.
`name.like('*guest*')`). Omitted entirely when unset; applies when draining and
when paging manually.
Example: `metadata.origin.eq('USER_DEFINED')`.

tools.name: query_teleport_invitations
tools.description:
List Teleport invitation history (v2 POST teleport/invitation-history).

Required: host and site. A read sent as POST (Consequence: none intended; it only
reads the history): it is not on the read-POST allowlist, so it is classed as a
write: UNIFI_WRITE_POLICY=deny refuses it, and under dry-run policy it returns a dry-run
preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path,
params, body}} of the first page and sends nothing.
Without a requested total every page is read (pageNumber 0, 1, ... to the end)
and the records are joined under data, adding _count and _pages; a stopped drain
(page cap, repeated page, a later page without records) adds incomplete: true and
incompleteReason. Returns that joined object. An empty first page is returned
verbatim; a first page without a data array is returned verbatim plus _pages and
_drainNote. page_number alone returns that page verbatim. page_size alone is window
0: exactly page_size records from record 0; _nextPage counts page_size windows, so
resume with page_number=_nextPage and the same page_size. page_number with page_size
returns that window. Omit both to drain every record.
_pageSize reports the requested count, sent (every pageSize sent, in request order),
the effective console page size and the returned count. _nextPage is absent when no
record follows the window or the call stopped incomplete.

Example call (query_teleport_invitations):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default"}

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or UUID, e.g. "Default".

page_number.description:
Zero-based page. With page_size, returns exactly page_size records
starting at record page_number * page_size, gathered across console pages
whatever the console page size; resume with _nextPage and the same page_size.
Without page_size, one request returns that console page verbatim. Example: 0.

page_size.description:
Number of invitations. Alone, window 0 (the first page_size records,
fewer only at the end); with page_number, the size of the window. Omit to
drain all. Example: `100`.

confirm.description: Ignored; accepted for compatibility. The call executes when made.

tools.name: remove_teleport_client
tools.description:
Remove a Teleport client (v2 DELETE teleport/client/{id}).

Consequence: the client loses Teleport access and must be invited again.
Required: host, site and client_id. No GET route lists Teleport clients by id, so
the id is sent as given and the controller judges it. body is optional and
free-form (the web app builds one; its shape is not published) and is sent
verbatim when given. Returns {deleted, message, response} with the upstream body
verbatim. Dry-run (dry-run policy) returns {status: "dry_run", deleted: false,
message, response}, where response is the dry-run preview {status: "dry_run",
dryRun, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}}; nothing is sent.

Example call (remove_teleport_client):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "client_id": "000000000000000000000107"}

Returns {deleted, message, response}: deleted is true, message summarizes the delete, and response is the upstream body verbatim (decoded JSON, raw text, or null when the body is empty).

host.description: Console name, MAC or id from list_hosts: reportedState.hostname/name (e.g. "my-console") or data[].id.

site.description: Network site name or UUID, e.g. "Default".

client_id.description:
Teleport client id from list_vpn_connections,
e.g. "000000000000000000000107".

body.description: Optional free-form request body, e.g. {"name": "guest-laptop"}.

confirm.description: Ignored; accepted for compatibility. The call executes when made.

tools.name: update_ipsec_settings
tools.description:
Update the site's IPsec settings (v2 POST settings/ipsec, read-merge-write).

Consequence: IPsec tunnels and remote IPsec users may reconnect.
Required: host, site and fields. Request body: no published schema; fields is

them. The current settings are read, your fields laid over them leaf by leaf and
the whole object POSTed. An empty update fails before any request. Returns the
upstream body verbatim plus _verified (type-strict leaf comparison of a
read-after) and _readAfter, or _readAfterError (a non-object write body is returned
whole under response with those keys beside it). Dry-run (dry-run policy) returns a
dry-run preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method,
path, params, body}}; nothing is sent.

Example call (update_ipsec_settings):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "fields": {"enabled": true}}

tools.name: update_radius_profile
tools.description:
Update a RADIUS profile via Classic REST PUT rest/radiusprofile/{_id}.

The published Integration API serves RADIUS profiles GET-only; this is the UI's route.
The id (list_radius_profiles id = external_id, or the Classic _id) is resolved in
rest/radiusprofile first (an unknown id fails listing every profile, no write is
sent). auth_servers / acct_servers replace the whole server list: send every server
to keep, each {ip, port, x_secret}.

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, {meta: {rc}, data: [the updated profile]}.
Additive _warnings (NO_ID_RETURNED, NOT_STORED_AS_SENT: field names only) report a
write that did not land as sent. Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the bare dry-run
preview {status: "dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path,
params, body}}.

Example call (update_radius_profile):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default",
     "profile_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
     "profile": {"interim_update_enabled": true}}

host.description: Console name (case-insensitive reportedState.hostname/name, e.g. "my-console") or data[].id (MAC:numericId), from list_hosts. Serves Network and Protect.

site.description:
Network site name or UUID; resolved server-side. Get it from list_local_sites
(name or id). Names like "Default" work.

profile_id.description:
RADIUS profile id from list_radius_profiles (data[].id) or its Classic
_id.

Native radiusprofile fields to change. Free-form JSON object; no published
body shape.

first; an unknown id fails listing every tunnel with both ids. Send only the fields to
change: the Classic PUT merges them into the stored record.

Returns: the upstream body verbatim, the Classic envelope {meta: {rc}, data: [the updated
networkconf record]}.
Under dry-run policy nothing is sent: the result is the bare dry-run preview {status:
"dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false,
message, preview: {method, path, params, body}} in place of the upstream body.

    {
      "host": "my-console",
      "site": "Default",
      "tunnel_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
      "tunnel": {"enabled": false}
    }

tools.name: update_wireguard_users
tools.description:
Update WireGuard users on one server (v2 PUT wireguard/{_id}/users/batch).

Consequence: changed keys or addresses disconnect the affected peers.
Required: host, site, server_id and users. Each users item names a user by _id
(from list_wireguard_users) plus only the fields to change (free-form; no
published schema). Every _id is resolved in the server's user list first; an
unknown _id fails listing every user and nothing is sent; an item with nothing to
change fails before any request. Each listed record with your fields laid over it
leaf by leaf is PUT as one array. Returns the upstream body verbatim plus
_verified (type-strict, every requested leaf of every user) and _readAfter, or
_readAfterError (a non-object write body is returned whole under response with those
keys beside it). Dry-run (dry-run policy) returns a dry-run preview {status:
"dry_run", dryRun: true, sent: false, message, preview: {method, path, params, body}}.

Example call (update_wireguard_users):
    {"host": "my-console", "site": "Default", "server_id": "000000000000000000000107",
     "users": [{"_id": "000000000000000000000108", "name": "laptop-02"}]}

site.description: Network site name or UUID, e.g. "Default".

server_id.description:
WireGuard server id from list_vpn_servers or its Classic _id,
e.g. "000000000000000000000107".

users.description:
Non-empty array of _id plus fields to change (an empty list fails before any
request), e.g. [{"_id": "000000000000000000000108", "name": "laptop-02"}].
Shape: {_id:string,...}[]; the other keys of each entry are the fields to change

confirm.description: Ignored; accepted for compatibility. The call executes when made.
